articleTitle: Survey on Protocols and Standards Used by Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: As the global need for sustainability and reduced carbon emissions has amplified, the automotive industry has witnessed a major push in the manufacturing of electric vehicles. The rapid increase in EVs has made it indispensable to use standardized protocols, as they play a vital role in coherent communication, safety, and efficiency. This paper examines the primary EV protocols that align with national and global standards. By analyzing standards such as ISO 15118, CHAdeMO, and OCPP, this study provides insights into the evolution of EV protocols aimed at interoperability and safety.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of MIMO Antenna for Enhanced 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper introduces the isolation enhancement technique for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1} \times \mathbf{2}$</tex> slot loaded MIMO antenna by using minimized ground plane. The proposed antenna is designed on a 1.5mm thick Taconic RF-35 substrate, operating at 4.8 GHz frequency). Inter-element spacing is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{0.105}\boldsymbol{\lambda}_{\mathbf{0}}(\mathbf{6.5}\text{mm})$</tex>. For isolation enhancement here ground plane is minimized. Two stages (Design-1,2) of the proposed MIMO antenna are compared. After the simulation Design-2 MIMO antenna is isolated more than 30dB. Other parameters, Envelope correlation coefficient (ECC) is 0.0001 and Diversity gain (DG) is closed to 10dB has been investigated in this paper. This MIMO antenna is convenient for 5G applications (5G NR band n79 4.4 GHz - 5 GHz frequency).

articleTitle: Analysis of Bit Rate vs SNR in Coded FSO Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The main requirements for a future communication system are low complexity, stronger performance, data processing, and higher data rate. These requirements have been fulfilled by Free Space Optical (FSO) communication systems. FSO is a visible or wireless light communication (WLC) system. Performance analysis itself is a critical stage in the field of FSO/ wireless communications due to the nature of multi-path fading that is encountered due to scatters. The BER performance depends on the employed detection scheme, signal-to-noise ratio (SNR), and diversity order. The main basic components for selecting channel coding techniques are Bit Error Rate (BER) and SNR. This paper examined the performance of different channel coding schemes including convolutional coding, LDPC (low-density parity check) coding, TCM (trellis coded modulation) coding, and concatenated coding schemes during diverse turbulence conditions using the log-normal and gamma-gamma distribution model in MATLAB. Simulation results and performance evaluation in terms of bit rate indicated that the concatenated coding scheme outperforms the other single channel coding schemes under various turbulence conditions.

articleTitle: Reconfiguring Multidimensional PV Arrays for Optimizing Output Power Under PSC
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: A solar photovoltaic (PV) power system consists of multiple modules connected in parallel and series to achieve a desired range of output voltage and current. However, these modules are highly vulnerable to partial shading condition(PSC), a common issue that can cause considerable power loss, hotspots, reduced system performance, and even permanent damage to the modules. To address these challenges, reconfiguration techniques are employed to redistribute shading intensity across the modules, reducing current mismatch and enhancing the system's power output. Despite their benefits, these techniques have a major limitation: they are predominantly designed for symmetrical or square arrays, which are uncommon in real-world applications. To increase system output power under different partial shading scenarios, this paper presents a Multidimensional Array Reconfiguration(MAR) technique for modules in asymmetrical arrays. The suggested methodology uses a one-time module arrangement and is simple, affordable, and easy to implement. In situations involving partial shading, it achieves lower power losses and improved system dependability.

articleTitle: Cramer-Rao Bound for SNR Estimation of Hyper-Cubic Signals Over Gamma Channel
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper presents the derivation of an analytical expression for the Cramer-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) on the variance of unbiased, non-data-aided (NDA) signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) estimators for hyper-cubic modulated signals. The analysis assumes Gamma noise (GN) channel model. It is demonstrated that, in the low-SNR regime, the CRLB varies significantly based on the hyper-cubic constellation (HCC) dimensionality and the number of observations. For higher-dimensional constellations, the CRLB is initially large but decreases substantially with an increasing number of observations. Conversely, in the high-SNR region, this behavior is reversed. Analysis of the data-assisted (DA) CRLB and NDA-CRLB for square quadrature amplitude modulation at more than one level and HCC respectively, reveals that their estimation variance characteristics converge toward comparable behaviour under high-SNR conditions.

articleTitle: Car Damage Identification System Using Convolutional Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The number of individuals driving has increased daily, leading to a rise in the number of auto insurance claims. The lengthy process of registering, processing, and determining the outcome of each claim includes the service engineer's manual assessment, which serves as the basis for the damage report, and the physical examination carried out by an insurance company surveyor. It would be advantageous for both the organization and the client if this entire procedure were automated. This system utilizes images of the car in a damaged state as input. It then generates pertinent data, including the locations of the damaged sections (front, rear, and sides) and an assessment of the extent of the damage (none, minor, or substantial). This system uses the Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) Model to analyze images automatically for auto insurance, providing the user with information on the location and extent of the vehicle damage. ImageNet weights and the VGG16 architecture are also used here. Transfer learning is used for a variety of tasks, such as finding and classifying different kinds of auto parts and issues. The logistic regression classifier is trained using feature and label extraction methods.

articleTitle: Frequency regulation of standalone microgrid Using MRFO algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: In the present work, Manta Ray Foraging Optimization (MRFO) algorithm optimized Proportional-Integral (PI) controller is studied for frequency adjustment of a standalone micro grid (MG). The MG system consists of a Diesel Engine Generator (DEG), Fuel Cell (FC), Micro Turbine (MT) through PI controller and photovoltaic (PV) systems with maximum power point trackers (MPPT) through another PI controller. The best gain values of the PI controllers are searched by MRFO algorithm using an Integral Time Absolute Error (ITAE) as fitness criteria. The simulation is carried out with different case studies. When compared to the results of other optimization approaches for the same MG, like Swalp Search Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization(PSO), and Teaching Learning Based Optimization(TLBO), the MRFO-based PI controller outperforms them in all scenarios. According to the simulation findings, the MRFO technique gives better dynamic responses in terms of overshoot, undershoot value, settling time, and Integral Time Absolute Error.

articleTitle: Thermoelectric Generator Employed Solar PV Hybrid System Considering Interconnection Schemes
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Research on thermoelectric generator (TEG)-based systems is gaining prominence due to the rising need for effective energy harvesting from renewable resources. These systems are essential for promoting sustainability and reducing fossil fuel reliance. A significant area of study is the integration of TEG with solar photovoltaic (PV) systems to enhance energy output. In a hybrid solar PV and TEG system, researchers analyzed the temperature distribution on the semiconductor plate using the constant variation approach. This method helps determine the optimal operational temperature for maximum power production, crucial for designing efficient energy systems. The study also examines the behavior of the hybrid system by coupling eight solar PV modules in different configurations, assessing their performance under Healthy Irradiance (optimal sunlight) and Sectional Irradiance (variable sunlight conditions). One key finding is that the efficiency of solar PV modules decreases with increased sun concentration, posing a challenge for solar PV technology. However, TEG systems benefit from higher sun concentration, experiencing increased output and efficiency. This contrasting response makes TEG systems a valuable addition to hybrid energy setups. The research underscores the potential of combining TEG and solar PV technologies to create more efficient renewable energy systems. By understanding temperature dynamics and optimizing system configurations, the overall performance of these hybrid systems can be enhanced, contributing to the development of sustainable energy solutions.

articleTitle: A Compact Dual Band Circularly Polarized Planar Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The current investigation presents a dual-band antenna characterized by circular polarization and high gain. The final antenna provides impedance bandwidth (2.5 - 4.45) GHz and (5.8 - 10.2) GHz. The 3 dB axial ratio (AR) bandwidth spans (2.9 - 3.3) GHz and (9.6 - 10.15) GHz. Furthermore, the designed antenna provides a narrow AR bandwidth (7.7 - 7.85) GHz. The proposed antenna is capable of radiating a LHCP wave in the upper frequency range and a RHCP wave within the lower frequency range. The 3 dB AR bandwidth is realized through the strategic placement of two rectangular cuts at the opposite corners of the modified ground plane, truncation of the opposite corners of the radiating element, as well as embedding two opposite C-shaped metallic strips in the ground. The antenna's peak gain in the desired band extends from 7.57 dBi to 11.24 dBi. The suggested antenna is compatible with IEEE 802.16a application requirements.

articleTitle: Smart Grid-Optimized Bidirectional EV Charging: A Hybrid Metaheuristic Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Smart grid with electric vehicle (EV) integration changes the pace of the new age power system. The bidirectional power flow is the major pros of modern smart grid. When EV connected to the local home electrical grid, the charger functions using a metaheuristic control. Additionally, the charger is constructed and maintained to function effectively under EV-smart grid integration. Electric vehicles' (EVs’) ideal charge-discharge performance is one way to improvise such consumer involvement. For the best performance of EVs in smart grid, this research presents a hybrid Meta heuristic approach that clubs the gravitational search algorithm and particle swarm optimization. Matlab/Simulink is used to simulate the entire system, and the outcomes of each case's operation are displayed along with a management system for these various working scenarios. The review and evaluation of the simulation results demonstrate that they adhere to current requirements for power quality.

articleTitle: An Improved Fast Decomposition-Instantaneous Power Theory Based Inverter Control Strategy for Grid Connected PV System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: During faults, voltage sag or contingencies occur on the grid side, it is essential to track the behavior of grid current instantly so that the associated inverters can initiate their control operation immediately. This paper gives insight into an improved inverter control strategy based on Fast Decomposition-Instantaneous Power Theory (FD-IPT) for a grid-connected photovoltaic (PV) system. In this proposed work, the IPT has been chosen to track down the active and reactive power on the instant from the grid response rather than waiting for the average power or a full cycle of completion. Further, the decomposition of the grid current into α-β components followed by time domain positive and negative sequence components in a faster manner helps to extract the instantaneous active and reactive power (PQ) from the ac grid and initiate the instant operation of the inverter. The proposed test system has been prepared in MATLAB/Simulink R2021a environment and validated the test response accordingly.

articleTitle: State-of-Charge Estimation of Lithium Battery Using Adaptive Extended Kalman Filter With LMAT Driven Parameter Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Accurate estimation of State-of-charge (SOC) act as a decisive factor for the management of lithium batteries, especially in applications like energy storage system (ESS), electric vehicles (EV) and portable electronics devices. Recently, model-based SOC estimation gained popularity due to their easy implantation and capability to capture the dynamic characteristics of the lithium battery. However, in model based SOC estimation, the battery model parameter tends to vary with the change in operating temperature. This variation in battery model parameter, affects the estimation accuracy of the filter significantly. In view of this, a least mean absolute third (LMAT) based adaptive extended Kalman filter (AEKF) is designed and proposed in this article. In the proposed method, the dynamic model parameter of the battery are estimated with a computationally efficient LMAT-based estimator and the battery SOC is estimated by adaptive correction of noise covariance matrix using AEKF. The SOC estimation accuracy of the proposed LMAT-based AEKF is examined by applying load current of the LA92 and US06 driving schedule at 0°C and 25°C respectively. Further, the performance indices of the proposed estimator are compared with other Kalman filter based SOC estimators available in the literature. The results confirm high SOC estimation accuracy of the proposed LMAT based AEKF compared to other KF based estimators with a root mean square error of less than 2% under dynamic operating condition.

articleTitle: Design of a Solar-Powered Remote-Controlled Aquatic Cleaning Drone
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The Remote-Controlled Solar Lake Pool Cleaner Drone is an innovative solution designed to automate the cleaning process of large bodies of water, such as lakes and pools, using renewable solar energy. This drone combines the advantages of remote control functionality, efficient cleaning mechanisms, and environmentally friendly power sources to provide an effective and sustainable solution for maintaining water cleanliness. The drone is equipped with advanced cleaning mechanisms, including a suction system and a brush mechanism, capable of efficiently removing debris, leaves, and algae from the water surface. Its remote-control capabilities allow operators to maneuver the drone effortlessly, enabling precise navigation and targeting specific areas requiring cleaning.

articleTitle: Technoeconomical Analysis of Grid Connected PV System Powered by Battery Implemented in Educational Institute
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The increase in energy demand and environmental pollution necessitates the integration of renewable energy sources with the grid. The hike of installation cost of the conventional photovoltaic cells causes to look for better optimized solutions to integrate the PV, energy storage devices and converters with the grid. In this paper the solar PV, energy storage devices are optimized and integrated with grid with reduced NPC (Net Present Cost) and COE (Cost of Energy) in HOMER PRO software to find out the most economically viable solution. Among all the configurations proposed, PV/Grid/Battery system emerges as the most economically viable solution. This system has an NPC of $4.906967 million, a COE of $0.09973, and an overall operating cost of $3.79433 million. The payback period of the above configuration is 7.2 years which is sufficient to recover all the capital cost.

articleTitle: Enhanced Power Quality with PV-Driven Active Power Filter in Two-Area Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The proposed study presents an advanced PV driven active power filter (PV_APF) based adaptive coordinated control (ADCA) controller aimed at optimizing power flow and improve the power quality (PQ) in large-scale power systems. To offer excellent transient support and provide faster action, a transient control unit (TCU) is also associated with the proposed ADCA. In addition to that, a transient detection unit (TDU) has developed to isolate the PV generation from the main grid within 8-10sec and uses the APF full capacity to provide the desired reactive power, which effectively eliminates the power instability. Moreover, for smooth power transition, a ramp based improved real power recovery strategy (IRPRS) is proposed to restore the PV power output incrementally after the minimization of transient, which improves the settling time as per the standard grid code requirement. During night, the full capacity of APF is applicable for transient mitigation, where as partial shading condition, the APF is applicable for maximum power extraction and stabilize the power fluctuations. The overall system performance is validated through simulation platform at a wide range of possible test cases. The outcomes ensure 24/7 support by delivering substantial enhancements in power transfer capability, enabling stable operation during both local and inter-area oscillations.

articleTitle: Real Time Implemenatation of Passive Cell Balancing and Verification of MIL and SIL in MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: In modern day electric vehicle battery is heart, to improve the life of battery is challenge this can be done by different method like cell balancing, either by dissipating heat through resistors or giving charge from one cell to another cell. This paper gives exact topology and real time implementation of passive cell balancing and verification of cell balancing using model in loop (MIL) and software in loop (SIL) using MATLAB. This paper present passive cell balancing circuit and its implementation using MATLAB. How resistors are acting as reactive component in passive cell balancing that is discuss. Balancing takes one by one for each cell. Cell balancing is done during charging time and while doing cell balancing continuously current is monitor. Modern tool is used to verify the BMS i.e. MIL and SIL, once MIL & SIL is done hardware implement in hardware is very easy. In the present paper comparison of passive cell balancing and active cell balancing is done. The efficiency of passive cell balancing is 99%. In the present paper MOSFET is used as switch and to trigger MOSFET control technique is implemented.

articleTitle: Double Self-Lift (DSL) Cell Based High Gain Modified Quadratic Converter for Fuel Cell Application
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Fuel Cell(FC) has high energy conversion capacity compared to combustion engines. Fuel cells posses low voltage but are very effective in terms of clean energy sources. For wider range of operation FC needs a suitable gain DC-DC converter applicable for fuel cell electric vehicles. Here a high gain double self-lift (DSL) based DC-DC quadratic boost converter (DSL-QBC) has been proposed. The proposed (DSL-QBC) possesses the benefit of low input current stress and low voltage stress across the switch and high output voltage gain. This property of the converter assists in the synchronization of converter with FC for better output. Double self lift network is an inductor capacitor network which helps in uplifting the voltage gain. Double self lift network is integrated with the simple quadratic boost converter to create a hybrid circuit and the detailed analysis of DSL-QBC has been presented. The modification has been highlighted in the figures shown in paper and the results have been verified using Matlab simulation platform. The proposed circuit topology DSL-QBC has been designed for 150 Watts under steady state condition.

articleTitle: Study of a Single Source Based High Gain 25 Level Switched Capacitor Multilevel Inverter
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper presents an innovative 25-level Switched Capacitor Multilevel Inverter (SCMLI) topology, comprising 18 switches and 7 capacitors, which generates a boosted output voltage using only a single DC power source. The proposed circuit employs a systematic capacitor charging sequence, achieving an output voltage boosting factor of 12. The Half-Height modulation technique is utilized to enable lowfrequency switching in the inverter design. Detailed analyses of voltage and current stresses are provided. Furthermore, the paper analyzes total harmonic distortion (THD), Weighted Total Harmonic Distortion (WTHD) and lower odd harmonic under different loading condition. A comparative evaluation highlights the superiority of the proposed SCMLI in terms of reduced component count, enhanced boosting factor, and improved cost efficiency when compared to existing designs. The functionality and advantages of the proposed system are analyzed through Matlab/Simulink model. The results confirm the effectiveness of the SCMLI under resistive and resistive-inductive loads, demonstrating balanced selfcapacitor voltage levels throughout operation.

articleTitle: Mobile Healthcare Model for Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The research paper explores the transformative potential of mobile healthcare (mHealth) models in revolutionizing disease diagnosis, driven by advancements in AI and remote diagnostic tools. It emphasizes the critical role of early intervention in preventing health deterioration and guiding effective treatments through accurate diagnosis. The study draws insights from a survey conducted by Japan's Initiative on Rare and Undiagnosed Diseases (IRUD), highlighting the urgent need for improved diagnostic tools, particularly for elderly individuals who face challenges accessing healthcare. It advocates for developing technological solutions for remote diagnosis, leveraging AI—especially Deep Learning—to provide precise insights that enhance healthcare outcomes. The paper outlines a detailed methodology for implementing mobile healthcare, including user account setup, health record management, symptom evaluation, and proactive guidance. It also stresses the importance of robust data handling practices, covering security, privacy, and compliance measures, while emphasizing ethical considerations in using mobile health data for research. By reviewing existing surveys and literature, the paper underscores the growing significance of mHealth in early disease detection and management. Ultimately, it proposes a comprehensive model to leverage mobile healthcare for transforming disease diagnosis and improving health outcomes.

articleTitle: Enhancing Power Quality in Solar-Integrated Smart Grids for EV Systems Through Smart Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Global need for Electric vehicles (EVs) is uninterruptedly growing, as a result of increased CO2 emissions and the harm that traditional cars cause to the environment. The transportation sector has also changed as a result of EVs. Because of its unique features, which include reduced carbon emissions, noise pollution, and operating costs, as well as the ability to function in dual Grid-To-Vehicle (G-V) & Vehicle-To-Grid (V-G) situations, EVs are becoming more and more popular. However, it has a variety of impacts on distributed grid. The addition of EVs to the distribution system has resulted in a number of power issues, including voltage oscillations, distortions in currents, harmonic distortions, and power factor degradation. This study's main focus is on reducing PQ problems, like as harmonics, that arise in the distributed power network when electric vehicles are incorporated at the distribution end. Using a Dynamic Shunt Filter (DSF) with MPSO tailored CCC control approach, the current profile on the distribution side is improved and harmonics are reduced. MATLAB/Simulink is used to validate MPSO-DSF performance in conjunction with VtoG and GtoV operations.

articleTitle: Enhanced Breast Cancer Detection Using Microwave Imaging with Patch Antenna Arrays and Delay-and-Sum Reconstruction
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This study investigates the application of microwave imaging for breast cancer detection, focusing on the use of a patch antenna array to enhance tumor identification. To simulate biological tissues, we designed a custom breast phantom consisting of specialized gels that mimic the dielectric properties of the human breast. Additionally, hydrogel balls immersed in water were used to represent tumors, providing a realistic test environment. We evaluated the effectiveness of both four-element and six-element patch antenna arrays in detecting the presence of tumors, comparing their performance in terms of sensitivity and resolution. The results demonstrated that while the four-element antenna array provided limited visibility of the tumors, the six-element array significantly improved detection capabilities, allowing for clearer imaging of the tumor locations. To reconstruct the microwave images, we employed the Delay-and-Sum (DAS) algorithm, which enhanced the spatial resolution and contrast of the images, facilitating more accurate tumor identification. The improved image quality obtained with the six-element array suggests that antenna configuration plays a crucial role in the efficacy of microwave imaging for breast cancer detection. This study underscores the potential of microwave imaging as a non-invasive, cost-effective, and promising technique for early breast cancer diagnostics, with significant implications for clinical applications.

articleTitle: Enactment of Deep Reinforcement Learning Agent for Duty Ratio Control of Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper presents a deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agent for duty ratio control of the dual active bridge (DAB) converter using triple phase shift (TPS) modulation. The operation of a dual active bridge under the TPS modulation technique was briefly discussed, stating its advantage over the other phase shift techniques, thus creating the requirement of a model-free control approach for the converter. The reinforcement learning method has evolved as the deep reinforcement learning method that can solve complex problems with rising computational accuracy. This paper focuses on a deep deterministic policy gradient (DDPG) agent founded on actor-critic policy, i.e. implemented as the DRL controller. A detailed discussion about the control strategy using the DRL controller was presented. The model was simulated using MATLAB/Simulink software version 2024b to verify the voltage regulation of the dual active bridge using the DDPG agent. Finally, the conclusion presents the advantages of using a DRL controller for the TPS modulation of the DAB converter.

articleTitle: Using Gamification to Reduce Youth Depression: A Step-by-Step Method
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Youth depression is a major global health concern due to its alarmingly high occurrence and harmful impact on mental health. Traditional therapy methods frequently struggle with involvement, accessibility, and stigma. This research addresses depression in young people by proposing a novel solution based on gamification concepts. Our method is based on creating a game module integrated with a ML model that is especially designed for young people with depression. It provides a fun and active way to reduce symptoms and postpone thoughts of suicide. The module includes a number of levels and activities that are meant to be enjoyable while also supporting mental and emotional health. Crucially, the game has an adaptable system that is connected to players’ depression levels, modifying job complexity in response to continuous evaluation to guarantee maximum effectiveness and engagement. The key component of our invention is the incorporation of a depression assessment question into the game interface, which allows users’ psychological states to be assessed in real time. The game's algorithm is informed by this data, which constantly adjusts the difficulty and intensity of the challenges to suit each player's demands. Our goal is to improve users’ feeling of agency and accomplishment by personalizing their gaming experience, which will have a beneficial effect on their mental health. Our work emphasizes the value of customized approaches in tackling the complex problems associated with depression and adds to the expanding corpus of research that examines the possibility of gamification in mental health therapies.

articleTitle: Flyback Converters for Electric Vehicle Applications- A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The operation of electric vehicles (EVs) is significantly influenced by power electronics. Out of all the power electronic converters, isolated converters are one of the vital components of EVs due to their efficient operation and safety features. The flyback converters are one of the simplest realizable isolated converters. Flyback converters have been used extensively in EVs. They are used in cell balancing applications, power trains, charger circuits, etc. There are many areas where the flyback converter is emerging as a viable option, when compared to existing isolated converter topologies. Despite this, there is a lack of literature that lists all applications together. In order to solve this, an effort has been made to gather the usage of flyback converters for EVs. The work describes the utilization of flyback converters for various EV applications, thereby providing a comparative analysis among the existing flyback converter based state-of-the-art topologies.

articleTitle: BPF Based SOGI Controller for Resolving Grid Side and Load Side Abnormalities in a Grid Interfaced PVG-UPQC System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: In a photovoltaic generator fed unified power quality conditioner (UPQC) system, the presence of grid side and load side abnormalities deteriorates the power quality of the grid current and load voltage. These abnormalities, which include DC offsets, higher order harmonics, and dominant lower order harmonics, lead to deviations from optimal performance and compliance with power quality standards. To address these challenges, this work proposes a bandpass filter (BPF) based second order generalized integrator (SOGI) control scheme. The presented control methodology is intended to effectively eliminate DC offsets, suppress higher order harmonics, and mitigate dominant lower order harmonics present in grid voltages and load currents. The effectiveness of the presented control methodology is examined using MATLAB/Simulink under various operating conditions, including harmonically distorted grid voltages, unbalanced load conditions, and variations in solar irradiation. Additionally, the presented controller's performance is compared with two existing approaches: a standard SOGI based UPQC and an enhanced SOGI based UPQC. The comparative evaluation demonstrates that the presented controller significantly reduces distortion in grid currents and load voltages. The proposed controller reduces total harmonic distortion in grid currents and load voltages, meeting IEEE Standard 519 limits and improving power quality in PVG-UPQC systems.

articleTitle: Flower Pollination Algorithm for Power Quality Enhancement in Smart Grids
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: In modern power systems, maintaining power quality has become a critical challenge, especially with the implementation of smart grids. Active Power Filters (APFs) are widely used to address these issues due to their ability to rapidly filter distortions and provide immediate compensation. To manage both voltage supply disturbances and load current variations, the Unified Power Quality Conditioner (UPQC) is commonly employed. The UPQC integrates both shunt and series active power filters in a unified system, utilizing a shared dc link capacitor. Effective regulation of the dc link capacitor voltage is crucial for the optimal performance of the UPQC. A PI controller typically used for this purpose. This study focuses on optimizing the PI controller parameters of the shunt active filter in the UPQC using the Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA) to enhance power quality. A MATLAB simulation model of a microgrid incorporating the UPQC was developed, and the results have been analyzed and discussed.

articleTitle: Innovative AI Approaches in Oral Proficiency Testing: Ethical Implications of ASR Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Oral proficiency testing plays a critical role in language assessment; however, classic ASR faces such problems as Americans Bias, which means difficulty for ASR as application to recognize non-American accents, and the evaluation inaccuracy. The major problem here is that classic ASR systems cannot recognize and assess non-American accents as they would reward non-biased, unbiased, and fair scores for speakers with regional or non-native English accents. This bias in particular distorts the fairness of the oral proficiency test. The current approaches are inefficient with regards to the fairness and standardization in natural language scenarios. Unfortunately, in practice the conventional ASR models are not perfect and become a source of errors and biases when trying to assign a score for the given speech; the specific problem with the current approach is that the speakers with regional or non-native accent will be almost impossible to score correctly. To address this bias, this study proposes BERTAdv, incorporating BERT which focuses on contextual understanding into the Adversarial training method for enhancing the ASR's accuracy in OPI. In an attempt to improve the BERTAdv to analyze both simple and complex linguistic attributes, the model is trained on a large and balanced dataset. The model presents desirable accuracy with a high R-squared of 0.93, MAE of 0.26, and RMSE of 0.46 and is more accurate and fairer than existing methods.

articleTitle: Stabilization and Performance Analysis of Double Link-Rotary Inverted Pendulum Using LQR-I Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper presents an optimal LQR-Integral based controller (LQR-I) for balancing control of the Double Link Rotary Inverted Pendulum (DL-RIP) system. It is one of the challenging topics in control and robotics due to its nonlinearity and instability, also complex system due to 3 degree of freedom rotary system. This system uses a motor to control and balance two rigid links serially connected pendulums in a vertically upward direction. Pole-zero mapping is used to determine the stability of the system. In this paper, a performance analysis of the system is done with an LQR-I controller using three reference paths (Square, Sawtooth, and Sinusoidal wave), two of which are discontinuous and one continuous path. The system shows less overshoot and deflection to stabilize the pendulum vertically upwardly with a continuous sinusoidal reference path compared to a square and sawtooth wave.

articleTitle: Minimum Variance Unbiased Estimators of Generalized Gaussian Distribution With an H-Proper Quaternion Random Variable
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive approach to parameter estimation in generalized Gaussian distributions (GGD) with -proper quaternion random variables, utilizing Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) and the Minimum Variance Unbiased Estimator (MVUE). These estimators provide a means to accurately capture the shape and scale parameters of quaternion-valued GGDs, which are increasingly relevant in multidimensional signal processing applications such as radar, sonar, and communications. By incorporating the Cramér-Rao Lower Bound (CRLB) as a performance benchmark, we assess the efficiency and effectiveness of MLE and MVUE in estimating GGD parameters within quaternion contexts. Our findings show that MLE achieves lower bias, especially with large sample sizes, while MVUE offers minimal variance, aligning with the CRLB. This study contributes to the development of robust statistical tools for quaternion-based data modeling, providing insights into efficient estimation techniques that support advanced signal processing tasks involving complex data structures.

articleTitle: Advances in Computational Epilepsy Diagnostics: Machine Learning at the Forefront
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Epilepsy is a prevalent neurological condition marked by spontaneous, recurrent seizures, significantly affecting quality of life and increasing mortality risk. This research paper delves into advanced computational methodologies for the detection and classification of epileptic seizures. Leveraging the power of machine learning and deep learning, this study aims to overcome the limitations of traditional diagnostic methods, which typically involve invasive monitoring and subjective analysis of EEG data. By introducing sophisticated machine learning models and employing non-linear classification techniques through kernel methods and support vector clustering, this research enhances the precision and speed of epilepsy diagnosis. The study not only explores the integration of these models into non-invasive, real-time monitoring systems but also discusses their impact on clinical practice and healthcare systems.

articleTitle: Power System Equipment Detection in Thermal Images by Deep Learning Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The non-contact accuracy of infrared thermography has made it indispensable for electrical equipment inspection. In order to recognize electrical equipment in thermal pictures, this study presents a revolutionary neural network-based learning model. Based on the neural network algorithm, the proposed work suggests a real-time object detection model YOLO-V8, that can predict the coordinate points, orientation angle, and type of class of certain equipment. To improve accuracy, particularly for small items, the model incorporates an orientation consistency prior. In the proposed work, an extensive thermal imaging dataset of a distribution transformer; covered a range of settings and equipment kinds. According to experimental results, the suggested model achieves a mean average precision of 93.7%, demonstrating its robustness to noise and ability to function at 20 frames per second resulting in accurate detection of different segments of a distribution transformer in a thermal image.

articleTitle: Enhancing Communication Infrastructure: PLCC for Underground Cable Networks
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Power Line Carrier Communication (PLCC) leverages existing power lines to establish communication between two points by transmitting higher frequency signals that are isolated from the power frequency using High Pass Filters or Capacitive Voltage Transformers (CVTs). This paper explores the application of PLCC technology in underground cable networks, where the inherent protection from environmental factors enhances communication reliability. A physical model has been developed, utilizing a 12V, 50Hz power signal and a 12V, 60kHz communication signal, with a modulation circuit based on the IC 555 timer to demonstrate data transmission over power lines. The experimental setup successfully isolates the communication signal from the power frequency, showcasing the potential of PLCC in underground cable systems. This research further proposes extending the capabilities of PLCC by increasing the communication frequency up to 800kHz, which would improve data transmission efficiency and expand communication bandwidth. The paper presents the practical implications of this approach for enhancing smart grid infrastructure, as well as its potential role in modernizing communication systems for urban power distribution networks.

articleTitle: Optimizing Regenerative Braking in Electric Vehicle: A Comprehensive Study of Control Strategies and Energy Recovery
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This study investigates the concept of regenerative braking in electric vehicles (EVs) and electric multiple units (EMUs), focusing on simulation and hardware in the loop (HIL) testing. This study analyses the power variation between non regenerative and regenerative braking modes, emphasizing the optimization of energy recovery and efficient power distribution. A two-stage control strategy that integrates field-oriented control for speed regulation and a DCDC converter for managing power between a battery and an ultracapacitor in a hybrid energy storage system (HESS) is proposed. The proposed system was validated through MATLAB simulations and HIL experiments, which demonstrated enhanced energy recovery, efficient load balancing, and improved battery protection. In addition, this study introduces a Mamdani fuzzy inference system for optimizing regenerative braking in fuel cell buses, considering safety, driving dynamics, and occupant comforts. The design of robust H∞ controllers further ensure system stability and minimizes disturbances during regenerative braking. The experimental results show that the H∞ controller outperforms traditional PI controllers in terms of energy recovery and dynamic response under various driving conditions. This study contributes to the advancement of regenerative braking technologies, offering insights into power system stabilization and energy conservation for both EVs and EMUs.

articleTitle: A Novel Method for Testing Digital ICs
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Digital Logic is the foundation of circuits and are used almost everywhere. The most commonly found and used digital logic are manufactured and used in the form of 16 pin DIP Package. The magnitude of its usage in both common and sophisticated electronics necessitates the verification of these ICs for their proper functioning. However traditional IC testers are often bulky as well as expensive and is not a popular option among hobbyists and small-scale industries. A novel and simple method has been employed to check these ICs in the form of Cloud Database Integration to check these ICs. The development of such an IC tester has been discussed in detail, highlighting all the aspects. This paper also explores all the benefits that are associated with this low-cost IC tester including accessibility and ease of use. Overall, this research paper aims to contribute in the field of IC testing by providing an efficient and feasible solution

articleTitle: Classification and Detection of Power Quality Disturbances using Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper explores the classification of power quality disturbances using machine learning models. It is started by generating signals that represent different types of disturbances and then processing them using Discrete Wavelet Transform with Daubechies wavelets to extract important features. A dataset has been created from these processed signals and used for training and testing with machine learning models. Among various techniques, Support Vector Machines (SVM) is opted for classification due to its accuracy and efficiency. Since power quality disturbances may lead to serious issues like system instability and equipment failure, having a reliable classification system is crucial. Here, SVM Kernel performs well while categorizing power quality disturbances.

articleTitle: Analysis of PI Speed Controller for Brushless DC Motors
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Brushless DC (BLDC) motors are among the most fascinating motors due to their efficiency and torque characteristics as well as the fact that they combine the advantages of a direct current (DC) supply with lack of the downsides related to brush usage. Due to the wide speedrange of BLDC motors, speed control is a crucial issue. A multitude of elements, including beginning current, starting torque, increasing time, etc., must be taken into consideration while analyzing the performance of a speed controller. The fundamental methods for controlling speed are fuzzy PI controllers and PID controllers. Both have various levels of intricacy and potency. For BLDC motors, this paper will provide PI speed controllers. For the purpose of assessing the effectiveness of the suggested speed controls, a simulation study is carried out.

articleTitle: Development of High-Efficient 3.7 kW 5 Level T-Type Inverter based Wireless EV Charging System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper presents the development and analysis of a high-efficiency 3.7 kW five-level T-type inverter designed for wireless electric vehicle (EV) charging applications. With a growing focus on sustainable energy solutions, the integration of photovoltaic (PV) systems into EV charging infrastructure has garnered significant interest among researchers. The proposed 3.7 kW five-level T-type inverter-based system facilitates the seamless integration of renewable energy sources, such as solar PV, while achieving high efficiency by minimizing switching losses typically associated with inverter operation. The charging system incorporates a series-series (S-S) compensation topology to ensure high power transfer efficiency and maintain stable performance under dynamic load conditions. A circular coil, specifically designed for this application, was analyzed using ANSYS Maxwell simulation to validate its theoretical characteristics. The system operates at a resonant frequency of 85 kHz, adhering to the SAE J2954 standard, and is optimized for a 3.7 kW power output. To evaluate its theoretical performance, the proposed system was simulated using the MATLAB/Simulink platform. Additionally, a 3.7 kW laboratory prototype was developed and tested experimentally. The results demonstrate the system's effectiveness and reliability, confirming its suitability for wireless EV charging applications.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Market-Clearing Methods in Community-Based Transactive Energy Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis of market-clearing methods in a community-driven transactive energy micro-grid aimed at enhancing community self-sufficiency, boosting self-consumption, and reducing costs for prosumers. The study explores various market-clearing approaches, including bill sharing, supply-to-demand ratio, and mid-market rate, to establish internal market prices for peer-to-peer energy transactions within the community microgrid. A deep learning algorithm is applied to forecast the participants' day-ahead demand and generation profiles. Simulation results demonstrate a marked improvement in self-sufficiency, higher self-consumption, and lower energy costs for participants across the community.

articleTitle: Analysis of ALFC in Two Area Power System Using Golden Eagle Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Automatic Load Frequency Control (ALFC) is used in interconnected power systems to control tie-line power flows and keep the system frequency within allowable bounds. This paper simulates and analyzes ALFC in a two-area power system using the Golden Eagle Optimization technique to stabilize frequency deviations when a load disturbance occurs. The proposed method utilizes different iterations and population sizes to obtain the optimal PID controller values for stabilizing frequency in both areas.

articleTitle: Smart Battery Swapping and Safety Management System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: In India the demand of EVs are continuously increasing as a necessity for the future, to efficiently implement this system we require proper charging infrastructure. To reduce the charging time of existing charging system we can use battery swapping system. This paper presents the development of a smart battery swapping system which is designed for two 3.7V 4Ah batteries. The system continuously monitors the SOC, battery temperature, and potential fire hazards. Using a DHT11 sensor for temperature tracking and flame detection, the system incorporates visual and audible alarms and relay control for safety. Additionally, the system sends SMS via SIM800L if any charging slot is empty, ensuring real-time management and efficient use.

articleTitle: Performance Comparison of SOGI and MSTOGI Based Phase Locked Loops for a DC Offset Perturbed Grid
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Nowadays, there is a lot of concern about ensuring that three-phase grid-connected renewable energy sources (RES) are properly synchronized. Key elements, including the utility voltage frequency, amplitude and phase, are essential for the suitable synchronization of grid-connected inverters. These factors are correctly determined in a Synchronous Reference Frame Phase Locked Loop (SRF PLL) under a perfect grid condition. However, its performance degrades in the presence of unbalanced or distorted grid conditions. As a result, there is a budding need for extremely efficient and accurate PLL system, for example the Dual Second Order Generalized Integrator PLL (DSOGI PLL), for grid synchronization. However, DSOGI PLL is unable to precisely estimate the phase when DC offset is present in the grid voltage, which calls for additional modifications. In order to find a better PLL with improved performances regarding adaptive filtering, DC rejection, and quickest transient response, this work explores an enhanced PLL based on SOGI filter modification and evaluates their benefits and drawbacks. The effectiveness of this enhanced PLL is analysed and validated through MATLAB/Simulink simulations under grid conditions affected by a DC offset.

Author Keywords: Mixed Second and Third Order Generalized Integrator (MSTOGI)

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of BLDC Motor Under Short Circuit Fault Condition
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper demonstrates a mathematical model and simulation of a Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motor, which is renowned for its high efficiency, power output, and low maintenance requirements. These advantageous features make BLDC motors prevalent in various advanced industries. However, faults or damage can degrade the motor's performance. The study focuses on the motor's behavior in both normal operation and under short-circuits fault conditions. A detailed comparison is made of the stator current and speed characteristics across the three phases, with the objective of assessing the motor's performance under different short-circuit fault scenarios.

articleTitle: An Efficient Deep Learning Approach for Food Quality Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This research aims to develop a deep learning system for assessing food edibility based on user-uploaded photos, addressing the global challenge of food waste. The system leverages the YOLOv8 model, renowned for its efficiency in object detection and classification, to evaluate visual attributes such as color changes, mold, and texture abnormalities, determining whether food is fresh or spoiled. With its advanced detection capabilities, YOLOv8 is well-suited for real-time classification, ensuring quick and accurate identification of spoilage across diverse food types and varying lighting conditions. Unlike traditional systems that often struggle with accuracy, especially when dealing with a wide variety of foods, this approach significantly enhances reliability. By enabling individuals to identify unsafe or spoiled food before consumption, this project contributes to reducing waste and promoting sustainable food practices while improving food safety.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Higher Order Sliding Mode Control for Grid Connected Shunt Active Filters with LCL Topology
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This study examines a three-phase, three-wire shunt active filter (SAF) integrated with the grid via an LCL filter, which mitigates distortions induced by the high switching frequency of the voltage source inverter (VSI) in SAFs. However, traditional linear feedback control methods for regulating the LCL filter introduce parasitic phase shifts between the reference and injected currents, reducing filtration efficiency. To address this, a sliding mode controller (SMC) is employed to minimize phase shift, enhance SAF performance, and improve resilience to system disturbances. Despite its advantages, SMC generates high-frequency switching signals that can strain VSI components. To overcome this limitation, a robust continuous higher-order sliding mode controller (HOSM) is implemented, utilizing pulse-width modulation (PWM) to maintain a stable and controlled switching frequency. The effectiveness of the proposed control strategy for industrial nonlinear loads is validated through simulations conducted in MATLAB and Simscape Power Systems.

articleTitle: Comparative Failure Rate Analysis of Dual Input Boost Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper proposes comparative analysis on the failure rate of the boost (BC) and the dual input interleaved boost converter (DIIBC) in accordance with the Military (MIL) handbook. Initially, the power loss and efficiency of both the converters are evaluated for the power rating of 1 kW under its normal operating conditions, and stress factor analysis is also tabulated. The failure rate of the power electronic components that are prone to failure using the MIL handbook is calculated and compared in the table. The results show that the dual input interleaved boost converter provides high reliability, power source stress, power source redundancy, high efficiency, low component stress, and scalability.

articleTitle: Improving Cervical Cancer Recurrence Prediction Through Multi-Source Data Integration and Advanced Deep Learning Approaches
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Cervical cancer recurrence prediction is a very crucial point in treatment because needing as much accuracy and speed as possible calls for better patient care. This research work presents the design of a high-performance predictive model that integrates multi-modal clinical data, such as imaging, genetic profiles, and health records of patients, to enhance accuracy in predicting recurrence. This can enable the capture of intricate factors of recurrence risk with the help of this kind of multimodal data integration. Deep learning techniques like convolutional neural networks and transformers are applied to each independent data source, with this model emphasizing attention mechanisms for interpretability that will inspire greater clinical trust and usability. In contrast to many conventional approaches that often use a single data source, this integrated methodology overcomes the critical limitations of using a broader spectrum of clinical inputs. It is further strengthened by data augmentation and generation of synthetic data, overcoming problems of data imbalance. Extensive validation on various datasets yielded a predictive accuracy of 95.7%, demonstrating its high performance. This holistic approach presented them with a valid and accurate method for predicting cervical cancer recurrence, thus equipping the clinicians with the necessary insight into informed decision-making that could lead to improved patient care and outcomes.

articleTitle: Utilization of Fully Transparent, Flexible, and Compact Modeled Low Voltage TFT for the Simulation of 2:4 and 3:8 Decoder Circuits
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This article presents the implementation of 2:4 and 3:8 decoder circuits using a previously simulated, low-voltage, compact-modeled, fully transparent, and flexible a-IGZO (amorphous-Indium Gallium Zinc Oxide)-based TFT device. The outputs for both decoders, ranging from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{D}_{\mathbf{0}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{D}_{\mathbf{3}}$</tex> for the 2:4 decoder and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{D}_{\mathbf{0}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{D}_{\mathbf{7}}$</tex> for the 3:8 decoder, were verified, demonstrating excellent transient characteristics in all cases. The compact modeling and circuit simulations were performed using Silvaco Techmodeler and Silvaco Gateway tools. Compact modeling with the Silvaco Techmodeler tool achieved high accuracy, with minimal error (less than 1%) between the modeled and simulated data. These decoder circuits show promise for future applications in complex memory circuits, display drivers, and control systems.

articleTitle: Sustainable Electric Power Transmission by Novel Quasi Opposition-Based Creation of Infrastructure and Enhancing the Quality of Education Based Algorithm: A Case Study on Vijayawada Region
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Sustainable electric power transmission by novel quasi opposition-based creation of infrastructure and enhancing the quality of education-based algorithm: a case study on Vijayawada region (QEIV) is applied for active power loss diminution and voltage stability expansion. The creation of educational organizations possesses multiple methodologies and mainly depends on the needs of the people in the region. Financial ability and availability of human resources are important in creating various educational institutions in the specific Vijayawada region. The assessment abilities of the members for the advancement of infrastructure are considered in the exploration section of the projected algorithm. In the process of amplification examination, stratagem is employed to augment the order of exploitation. Balancing the faculties, advancing the technology, acquiring the students' needs and improving the teaching standards of the institution from time to time are the factors which enable the excellence in quality of education. Sustainable electric power transmission by novel quasi opposition-based creation of infrastructure and enhancing the quality of education-based algorithm: a case study on Vijayawada region (QEIV) is validated in 7 benchmark functions, IEEE 30, 57 bus systems and 220Kv network.

articleTitle: Analysis of Effect of Fill Factor and Potential Induced Degradation on the Performance of Photovoltaic Module
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Solar energy is the cleanest form of energy which can be used in both ways like solar thermal and conversion to electrical energy as in case of photovoltaic system. The basic unit of solar PV system is a solar cell. Studies state that 32 to 36 crystalline cells are connected in series to form a module supplying 12 volt. Thus modules are the building blocks of solar arrays. There are different types of factor affecting performance of solar module. Irradiance, temperature, tilt angle, dust, shading are some of the major factors. Apart from this there are several other factors also which affect the performance of solar cell. Fill factor is the performance indicator of solar cell. Thus in this paper we have studied how fill factor affects the performance of solar cell. Even potential degradation is also another area which has been considered for study.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Task Master Robotic Arm Attachment for Enhanced Hammering, Cutting and Carving Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: In traditional industrial and construction settings, tasks like hammering, pipe cutting and stone carving often require specialized tools, each serving a distinct purpose. However, this approach can be inefficient, leading to increased costs and reduced productivity. To address these challenges, this project introduces a revolutionary concept: a single multifunctional tool designed to handle all these tasks seamlessly. All functions can be performed using a single piece of require manual labour, especially in small areas. The creative idea combines pneumatic technology with adaptable arm attachments to overcome these difficulties. These accessories are designed to increase productivity and accuracy in a variety of industrial applications like precise stone carving, accurate pipe cutting and effective hammering. It also decreases the meantime. Its ergonomic design ensures comfortable handling, while its robust construction enables it to withstand rigorous industrial applications. Moreover, intuitive controls and interchangeable attachments allow users to transition between different tasks effortlessly, further enhancing productivity. The technology runs on compressed air with minimum operator fatigue and constant performance. By embracing this multifunctional tool, businesses can streamline their operations, reduce equipment costs, and improve overall efficiency. This multifunctional tool represents a transformative innovation in industrial and construction practices, offering a comprehensive solution to the challenges posed by traditional methods.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Power Flow Solutions for Distribution Networks with Solar Energy Resources
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This article explores the efficacy of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to approximate the AC-power flow solutions for distribution networks (DNs) with solar energy resources. Generally, the power flow equations are non-linear and non-convex, making them difficult to solve directly. Traditionally, different classical linear algebra and heuristic search-based methods are developed to solve power flow problems, but those are difficult to implement for bulk radial distribution networks due to their complex and challenging mathematical formulations. Recent advancements in data-driven techniques, particularly neural networks, open the opportunity to tackle such complexities. In this regard, this article developed two ANN structures for determining the bus voltages, network loss, and substation power for radial DNs. Initially, a power flow dataset is synthesized by generating the load and solar power scenarios using Monte Carlo sampling followed by power flow calculation in OpenDSS. Later, the prepared dataset is implemented on the two developed ANN structures and the performance comparisons of them are provided for the IEEE 33 bus test system.

articleTitle: An Effective Web Page Recommendation System Techniques, Challenges and Future Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper explores advancements and future directions in webpage recommendation systems, a field central to enhancing user engagement and content relevance on the internet. Traditional recommendation approaches, such as collaborative and content-based filtering, have laid a strong foundation but exhibit limitations, particularly regarding personalization, scalability, and user privacy. Emerging technologies, including deep learning, graph neural networks, federated learning, and explainable artificial intelligence, offer new pathways to address these limitations. This paper reviews these technologies, examining their potential to improve recommendation accuracy, personalization, and privacy preservation. Furthermore, it highlights future directions that integrate hybrid recommendation techniques, context-aware systems, and ethical considerations, creating a blueprint for next-generation recommendation systems that align with user needs and societal values. This study provides a comprehensive analysis of how state-of-the-art techniques can transform webpage recommendations, setting the stage for further research and development in this rapidly evolving field.

articleTitle: Development of Neuro-Fuzzy Controller for Pressure Control of Artificial Respiratory System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Artificial ventilators or Mechanical ventilators (MVs) are critical medical devices used to support or replace spontaneous breathing in patients, particularly during surgical procedures or in ICU settings for those with respiratory distress. This study examines the functionality of a piston-driven ventilator, often utilized as an anesthesia ventilator operating in volume-controlled modes. Unlike traditional volume control, a pressure-controlled mode can be advantageous in specific scenarios, such as in laparoscopic surgery, by providing better compliance during pneumoperitoneum, enhancing oxygen delivery, and reducing stress post-surgery. Accurate pressure tracking is crucial in pressure-controlled ventilation (PCV) to minimize risks such as ventilator-induced diaphragmatic dysfunction. To address this, a neuro-fuzzy controller is proposed for precise pressure tracking in artificial ventilators. By integrating fuzzy logic and neural network elements, the neuro-fuzzy controller aims to maintain a responsive and adaptable pressure profile, tailored to the patient's needs. This study evaluates the controller's performance under various simulated scenarios, benchmarking its effectiveness against current methods in ventilator control

articleTitle: Emotion-Based Music Recommendation System Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Emotion-aware music recommendation systems have emerged as a promising approach to enhancing user experiences by tailoring music suggestions to emotional states. This paper presents a novel system that integrates facial emotion recognition and music recommendation, leveraging state-of-the-art deep learning and natural language processing techniques. Emotion recognition is achieved using fine-tuned ResNet50V2 and VGG16 models, which classify facial expressions with improved accuracy. For music recommendation, the system employs BERT to analyze song lyrics and metadata, enabling dy-namic alignment between user emotions and musical attributes such as tempo, mood, and lyrical themes. Experimental results demonstrate an emotion recognition accuracy and high user satisfaction in music recommendations. The system offers real-time contextual adaptation, ensuring seamless and personalized music experiences. Future directions include multimodal emotion detection and incorporating user contexts like location and activity for further personalization. This work highlights the potential of emotion-aware systems in revolutionizing music recommendation technologies,

articleTitle: Membership Function Shape Optimization of Fuzzy PIDN Controller Based on CTO to Track Output Power of PWR System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The shape of fuzzy membership function (MF) is important for performance analysis of any fuzzy inference system (FIS). Normally MFs are chosen by engineering knowledge and expertise but this may not reflect optimal performance in control problems. The aim of the paper is to present a method by using class topper optimization (CTO) algorithm to optimize the shape of membership function of FIS for PWR system. The method is basically to choose the correct membership function for the fuzzy PIDN controller to track output power of PWR system. The simulation result reflects good tracking performance in the proposed work.

articleTitle: Modified Sigma-Pi Neural Network for Dynamical System Identification
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This study introduces a newly developed Modified Sigma-Pi Neural Network (MSPNN) architecture designed to identify the dynamics of the plant. The proposed structure is an extension of the classical sigma-pi neural network (SPNN) and includes a self-feedback loop at the output node of the output layer. Since sigma-pi artificial neural networks contain additive and multiplicative units in their structure. We apply the back-propagation optimization algorithm to train the proposed MSPNN model. The results of the proposed neural network are compared with preexisting models, such as the Jordan neural network, the feedforward neural network, and the sigma-pi neural network. An analysis of the simulation data indicates that the proposed architecture of MSPNN is more effective than the other models.

articleTitle: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Tomato Leaf Disease Diagnosis: A Performance Comparison of DL Models
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Early prediction of the tomato leaf disease could benefit farmers in the agriculture field. It can reduce yield loss by detecting the disease promptly. This paper employed three distinct models of Deep Learning for the early prediction of the leaf disease, such models are Convolutional Neural Network, EfficientNetB3, and VGG16. This research article works on the classification of the various kinds of tomato leaf disorders, 10 different leaf disorders are used with a total of 10,000 images, and each disorder has 1000 images. Among the three models, the EfficientNetB3 model performed better with a testing accuracy of 98%, with a minimum testing loss of 0.041 loss. This model performed better because of its depth-wise, and widthwise scaling, and optimized compound scaling of the networks.

articleTitle: Voice Command Fingerprinting: An in-Depth Examination of Challenges and Issues
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Voice assistant systems have gained widespread adoption across diverse sectors, including electronics, healthcare, automotive, and retail. Spoken Language Understanding is essential for voice-text interaction systems. Security researchers have already identified vulnerabilities in encrypted network traffic, particularly in the context of traffic analysis, enabling the network-level adversaries to infer the websites visited by users. This security threat, common in traditional web communication, extends to Website Fingerprinting attacks in voice query communication, giving rise to the concept of Voice Command Traffic Fingerprinting. This paper analyses the features, challenges and linguistic properties of VCF(Voice Command Fingerprinting) considering various features. A detailed analysis reveals that the proposed models for voice command categories and factors are more capable to handle the issues. The results and methods in this paper pave the way for further research on the secured models in voice command processing in . The Python tools like Tensor-flow, Scikit-learn and specially Pyttsx3 have been used for generating and filtering datasets. An CTC-Attention-based hybrid model recurrent unit which effectively combine the two models. The proposed model achieves over 99.7% accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis of Isolated Bi-Directional CLLC DC-DC Converters for Fast Electric-Vehicle (EV) Battery Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Bidirectional onboard chargers play a vital role in electric vehicles (EVs), contributing to smart grid applications by enabling functions such as peak load management and supporting grid stability through frequency and voltage regulation. However, traditional full-bridge dual-active bridge (FBDAB) resonant converters commonly used in these systems face considerable efficiency losses, particularly during reverse power flow and when operating away from their resonant frequency-a condition often caused by fluctuations in battery voltage. To overcome these challenges, this paper presents a bidirectional battery charger based on a CLLC resonant converter with efficient tracking mechanism. The converter's steady-state behavior is analyzed under both grid-to-vehicle (G2V) charging and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) discharging conditions. By maintaining the switching frequency close to the ideal resonant point, this design successfully lowers circulating currents in the resonant tank and transformer, decrease losses in MOSFETs, and limits the rate of current change in the diodes. Simulations comparing this approach to a FBDAB resonant converter with fixed DC demonstrate the enhanced efficiency and superior performance of the proposed system.

articleTitle: A Laboratory Exercise for System Identification of Passive LTI System and its Dynamic Simulation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper outlines the crucial steps while performing system identification on a linear time invariant (LTI) passive equipment to obtain a model apt for dynamic simulation. The device under test (DUT) is a single-port voltage transducer. A concise overview of system identification methods is presented in this paper and later graduate towards frequency response estimation (black-box) approach. Using vector-fitting technique the experimentally obtained frequency response is transformed into a state-space representation which are readily used for dynamic simulations. The key assumptions considered in the paper while developing dynamic model are that the DUT is LTI and passive. Coherence as an indicator is used to assess the LTI nature from the input-output measurements. Similarly, passivity conditions are checked to assess model's passivity. The applicability of the developed dynamic model are highlighted. An experimental set of time-domain excitations is used to verify the simulated dynamic model. This exercise can be an effective laboratory course component, introducing students to essential concepts in system identification and dynamic simulation.

articleTitle: ICOA Based Load Frequency Control Optimized ITDF Controller Integrating Distributed Generation Resources
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
