abstract: The load frequency control of a multi-area system integrated with distributed generation resources are applied in this study using improved coati optimization algorithm (ICOA). Wind turbines' intermittent power output under frequent and economical load adjustments in distributed generation resources (DGR) contributes to tie-line power instability and system frequency ambiguity. Review the current electricity system's performance going forward, taking into account the integrated DG resources. A revolutionary integral of tilted derivative filter (I-TDF) controller is explored using ICOA for enhancement of frequency stability. Research shows that I-TDF performs better than other controllers in terms of lowering peak, settling time, and cost function value. The ICOA algorithm's superiority is contrasted with that of the sine cosine algorithm (SCA) and emperor penguin optimization (EPO).

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Power Efficient Four Phase Pipelined ALU
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This study explores the design and synthesis of a 4-phase pipelined Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) to boost computing efficiency. The pipelined architecture—comprising fetch, decode, execute, and write back phases—enhances throughput and re-duces latency by overlapping instruction executions. Designed using Hardware Description Languages (HDL) such as Verilog, the ALU is synthesized into a gate-level representation while adhering to timing, area, and power constraints. The results show that the 4-phase pipelined ALU significantly improves processing performance and efficiency.

articleTitle: VisMLB: An Hybrid Data Visualization Model for Major League Baseball Matches Using Tableau
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This manuscript provides an in-depth analysis of Major League Baseball (MLB) team performance from 2005 to 2023 using data visualization in Tableau and proposed an hybrid data visualization model (VisMLB) for Major League Baseball matches. The objective is to identify key metrics, such as batting, fielding, and pitching, that influence team success, including championship wins. The authors analyze the total number of championships won by each team, compare top-performing teams based on a variety of performance metrics, and explore the relationship between On-Base Percentage (OBP) and Slugging Percentage (SLG) for home and visitor teams in relation to home victories. Using Tableau, feature importance is visualized, and predictive models are evaluated for accuracy, precision, and recall. The findings offer a comprehensive overview of MLB performance trends over nearly two decades.

articleTitle: MUD in an Underwater Network Using Bioinspired Binary Tunicate Swarm Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: High data rate in underwater using acoustic waves is achieved through the implementation of multi carrier system. One such system considered in this research is multiple input multiple output (MIMO) orthogonal frequency division multiplexing (OFDM) system. The capacity of this considered system falls due to the interference from multiple number (No.) of users called multiple access interference (MAI) at its receiver. Therefore, such system at its receiver requires multiuser detection (MUD) in an underwater acoustic (UWA) environment. In this research, MUD is accomplished in an UWA network using global optimal solution obtained from jet propulsion and swarm behaviors of tunicates. The transceiver modelling of the considered system is done using World Ocean Simulator. The bit error rate (BER) analysis resulted from MATLAB simulation reveal that proposed binary tunicate swarm optimizer (BTSO) outperforms with best optimal solution over existing conventional approaches and bio-inspired optimizer such as BSHO and BPSO in binary domain based on the behavior of spotted Hyena and Particle Swarm respectively in an UWA network.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Network Security through Machine Learning and Deep Learning Techniques: A Real-Time Intrusion Detection System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Developing a resilient intrusion detection system (IDS) is essential to strengthen network security against advanced cyber threats. This project leverages machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques to create an IDS that surpasses traditional signature-based methods by detecting and mitigating attacks in real time. By analyzing abnormal patterns and recognizing attack signatures in network traffic, this system ensures a proactive defense mechanism. Utilizing the KDD 1999 dataset, a comprehensive benchmark for network intrusion detection, the IDS incorporates models such as Support Vector Machines (SVM) and XGBoost (XGB) for high-precision classification and regression tasks. Data preprocessing techniques like Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and RobustScaler enhance scaling, while classifiers such as Decision Trees (DT), Random Forest(RF) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) improve detection accuracy. Model performance is evaluated on metrics such as accuracy, precision and recall scores to ensure reliable detection of diverse intrusion types. By integrating ML and DL, this project demonstrates the power of scalable, real-time detection methods capable of identifying novel attack patterns, marking a significant advancement over static, traditional detection systems.

articleTitle: Implementation of Digital Logic Gate Families Using Low Operating Flexible Organic TFT Based on Innovative Compact Modeling Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The article demonstrates the brief fabrication method of the flexible organic thin film transistor (OTFT) developed earlier and its utilization for the development of various basic logic gates (NAND, NOR, AND, NOT, and OR Gates). The compact modeling of the fabricated device and the implementation of the logic gates has been carried out using Silvaco-Techmodeler and Silvaco-Gateway tools, respectively. The device can operate at -2 V supply with good electrical characteristics in terms of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-2\mu \mathrm{A}$</tex> drain current, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{ON}}/\mathrm{I}_{\text{OFF}}\sim 10^{3}$</tex> ‘ and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu_{p}\sim 0.1\text{cm}^{2}/\mathrm{V}-\sec$</tex> respectively. The Silvaco-Gateway tool implements the logic gates with excellent characteristics, demonstrating logic swing of 1.18 V and a delay of 3.7 ns. The logic gates also possess a good transient characteristic with all four possible logic inputs (00, 01, 10, and 11). The Silvaco-Techmodeler tool models the device with an accuracy of approximately 100%, with a 0.07% and 0.08% error between the experimental and modeled data, respectively. The cost-efficiently fabricated solution-processed transistor in this article can be further utilized in the fields of medical and sensing applications.

articleTitle: MobileNetV2: A Lightweight Solution for Orange Leaf Disease Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Orange leaf disease is one of the major risks to global citrus output, and for this reason, there is an urgent need to develop prompt and accurate detection techniques to minimize the effects of this disease. Traditional approaches used to detect unhealthy citrus plants are sometimes time-consuming and prone to errors. Recent advances in deep learning offer very accurate methods of automated disease identification. This paper introduces a model called MobileNetV2. It is designed to identify the orange leaf disease in citrus leaf photos. The proposed model uses a sequential architecture with several convolutional layers, batch normalization, max pooling, and dropout techniques to improve feature extraction and boost classification accuracy. This model demonstrated its ability to discriminate between healthy and diseased citrus leaves through extensive testing on a diverse dataset of images of citrus leaves, resulting in an accuracy of 98.21%. Batch normalization coupled with dropout improved the robustness of the model and its generality heavily. The results highlight the ability of the model to provide efficient, scalable, and reliable means of quickly detecting orange leaf disease.

articleTitle: A High Gain Multi Stage, Multi Device DC-DC Boost Converter Using Improved Switched Inductor Network for Solar PV Application
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-device improved switched inductor-based DC-DC boost converter (MDISIBC). The improved switching inductor and multi-device units make up the suggested structure. The proposed structure significantly magnifies the versatility in selecting the desired voltage gain by adjusting the number of inductors, switches, and the duty ratio (D). This improved switched inductor network enables a enhanced voltage gain, while the multi-device configuration helps minimize the ratings of passive components. The suggested paper presents the derivation of a generalized structure for a k-stage improved switched inductor network with m active switches (multi-device). The operation of the proposed converter in continuous conduction mode is discussed. Moreover, a comparative performance of the proposed converter with other existing high gain DC-DC boost converter is presented. The proposed converter with a parameter 200w,24/120V is validated by using MATLAB/Simulink. The results of the simulation demonstrated that the suggested converter is more effective than existing topologies already in achieving high performance.

articleTitle: Ensemble Learning for Enhanced Fault Classification in Smart Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: With the developments in Deep Learning algorithms, researchers have been turning to neural network-based approaches for detection of transmission line faults. However, deep learning methods necessitate a huge data to train properly. Furthermore, they have much less interpretability than traditional machine learning models. Here, some of the most popular ensemble learning techniques are compared for classification of transmission line faults. The study compares Random Forest, XGBoost and AdaBoost. The training data was generated using a 6 bus IEEE system simulated in MATLAB. The data thus obtained was pre-processed and relevant features were extracted from it before training the models. The study shows that AdaBoost performed better than the other classifiers, achieving an accuracy of 99.46%, thus establishing that traditional machine learning models are still relevant.

articleTitle: Design Algorithms for Lifelong Learning That Maintain Performance on Old Tasks While Learning New Ones
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Lifelong studying, or persistent learning, seeks to enable synthetic intelligence (AI) systems to accumulate knowledge and skills over the years even as preserving performance on formerly found out tasks. A number one challenge in lifelong learning is the stability-plasticity catch 22 situation: how to strike a stability among retaining old knowledge (stability) and integrating new understanding (plasticity). This paper explores algorithmic strategies for lifelong studying, that specialize in mitigating catastrophic forgetting and improving understanding switch across tasks. We present a complete evaluate of current strategies, suggest novel strategies, and compare their effectiveness in benchmark environments. By addressing center challenges, this study contributes to advancing the improvement of robust and adaptive AI structures able to lifelong mastering.

articleTitle: Lithium-ion Battery Modeling and HIL Testing With OPALRT
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Battery modeling plays a crucial role in understanding and enhancing the performance of lithium-ion batteries, especially for applications like electric vehicles. Such models are essential for tasks like state estimation, performance prediction, and system control, all of which contribute to safer and more efficient battery usage. This work aims to develop a reliable model of a lithium-ion battery by first estimating key parameters through the least squares method using MATLAB's parameter estimation tools. With these parameters, a detailed model is developed in MATLAB Simulink that accounts for important effects like hysteresis. The model's accuracy is then assessed by testing it at various temperatures (15°C, 25°C, and 45°C) to observe changes in performance under different thermal conditions. Finally, the hardware realization of the developed battery model is obtained using Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing on the OPAL-RT platform, which allows for real-time validation and provides a strong foundation for future research in battery management applications.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Machine Learning Approach for Prediction of Road Accident Severity
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Road accidents are a primary global concern for public safety, with India having a very high death toll. This study presents an intelligent machine learning approach to predict the severity of road accidents, contributing to the development of more effective and preventive measures. We utilized a comprehensive dataset of road accidents in India, employing advanced machine learning algorithms, including Histogram-based Gradient Boosting (HGB), Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machines (SVM), and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN). Our methodology involved extensive data pre-processing, feature engineering, and model optimization. The Random Forest algorithm demonstrated superior performance, achieving an accuracy of 94.7% and an F1-score of 0.947. This research provides a robust predictive model and information on the key factors influencing the accident's severity. The novelty of our approach lies in the comprehensive feature engineering tailored to the Indian context and the application of ensemble learning techniques to capture complex, nonlinear relationships in accident data. The findings of this study have significant implications for policymakers, urban planners, and law enforcement agencies in their efforts to improve road safety.

articleTitle: Modelling and Simulation of Lithium-Ion Battery with Thermal Dependence
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The growing demand for high-performance lithium-ion batteries in applications including power tools, grid storage, and electric vehicles calls for the creation of precise and trustworthy models for battery simulation and characterization. It emphasizes the need for precise models to simulate and characterize battery behavior. In this paper a comprehensive approach using a Three-Resistor-Capacitor (3-RC) equivalent circuit model to simulate lithium-ion batteries, focusing on their electrochemical charge/discharge mechanisms is presented. During a series of 31A discharge pulses, the cell potential decreases as the SOC started declining. The model effectively replicates capacity degradation, efficiency losses, and thermal management, contributing to safer, more durable, and efficient battery systems. The simulation successfully tracks open-circuit voltage (OCV) decline and replicates nine discharge pulses, demonstrating its accuracy in capturing system dynamics. The streamlined approach of the equivalent circuit model makes it an excellent choice when developing both control algorithms and system-level models. This simulation framework developed is an approach to optimize Li-ion battery management systems and to find means of advancement of future Li-ion technologies.

articleTitle: Non-linear Dynamic System Identification on Application of Industrial Control
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: System identification is a vital aspect of modern control and automation, offering a pathway to develop mathematical models from observed input-output data of dynamic systems. This paper explores methodologies, applications, and advancements in system identification. Applications such as digital twin integration, industrial automation, and transportation systems highlight the practical relevance of these methodologies. A focus is given to integrating advanced machine learning techniques with traditional modelling approaches to enhance accuracy and scalability for nonlinear dynamic systems. Deep Random Vector Functional Neural Network is used for experimentation. Practical applications, including digital twin integration for real-time monitoring and control, are discussed to underline the relevance of system identification in Industry 4.0.

articleTitle: Robust Channel Estimation in NOMA Systems Using Weinbull M- Transform for Adaptive Filtering
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This research paper explores the challenges of adaptive filtering methods used for channel estimation techniques in NOMA (Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access) systems within high-noise and dynamic environments. Conventional methods are often limited by high Bit Error Rate (BER), energy inefficiency, and reduced sum capacity, which can hinder their performance in modern, high-density applications like 5G communication. To address these limitations, the authors introduce the robust Weibull M-transform as an advanced solution for estimating the channel parameters in NOMA system. By incorporating exponential decay and adaptive scaling, this approach minimizes the impact of large scale errors, enhances stability, reduces BER rate, improves energy efficiency, and maximizes sum capacity-making it a strong candidate for use in demanding, contemporary communication networks where traditional methods are less effective.

articleTitle: Harmonic Reduction and Voltage Stabilization in Grid-Connected Photovoltaic Systems Using Z-Source Converters
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This This paper presents a detailed investigation into the performance and operational advantages of Z-Source Converters (ZSCs) in renewable energy systems, particularly focusing on photovoltaic (PV) applications. ZSCs, with their unique impedance network, offer a significant improvement over conventional voltage and current source converters by providing both buck-boost functionality without requiring complex control algorithms. The study examines the ability of ZSCs to enhance energy efficiency, reduce harmonic distortion, and improve voltage stability, making them well-suited for grid integration and battery management systems in electric vehicles. Simulations and comparative analyses between traditional converters and ZSCs demonstrate the superior performance of ZSCs, especially in maintaining consistent power output under variable load conditions. By incorporating ZSCs into renewable energy and electric vehicle systems, this research emphasizes their potential to facilitate higher efficiency and reliability, contributing to a sustainable energy future. A MATLAB Simulink model has been developed to address the proposed technique

articleTitle: A Review on Reactive Power Compensation Techniques in Grid-Integrated Photovoltaic System Using Facts Devices and Fixed Capacitor Bank
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Over the last decades, the generation of largescale electricity has increased considerably using renewable energy. This idea came to resolve the overwhelming electricity demand by consumers and to address the unhealthy climatic conditions amid power generation. With the advancements made in power electronic-based technology, solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems are massively synchronized with the electric grid to support the overall generation and to meet consumer demand. This improves the power generation to a larger extent. However, this technology faces challenges as conventional solar inverters only produce active power, whereas the grid requires active and reactive powers to address the intricate demands of loads and line parameters. This mismatch derails the voltage profile of the system. To maintain an acceptable voltage profile, reactive power compensation is important. Against this background, this paper reviews and compares several reactive power compensation techniques proposed in many literatures for grid-connected Photovoltaic power system operation. The paper considers seven methods proposed for load compensation with emphasis on the use of Flexible Alternating Current Transmission System (FACTS) devices.

articleTitle: Transformers with Temporal Enhanced Attention Over Graphs for Accurate Identification of Pancreatic Cancer
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: An aggressive from of cancer that rarely shows symptoms in its early stages and hence can be diagnosed at an advanced stage. CT scan or MRI is used to diagnose it in the early stage because early diagnosis gives higher chance of surviving. This work presents an innovative approach to applying deep learning to early pancreatic cancer detection, termed the Transformer-Enhanced Dynamic Spatial-Temporal Graph Network (TED-STGN), which combines Graph Neural Networks (GNNs), Transformer-based self-attention mechanisms, and spatial-temporal analysis to detect the tumour's progression in a series of medical scans. TED-STGN builds a kinetically changing spatial-temporal graph from medical imaging data where each image frame of a video is split into regions that will be the nodes of the graph. The graph attention mechanism controls the dynamic attention distribution for regions which have more apparent changes over time such as tumor area growth. The model uses transformer layers to apply models which capture long-range dependencies between frames and are capable of tracking temporal shifts that mark the initial onset of pancreatic cancers. Furthermore, another enhancement of this model is the self-supervised pre-training phase, which allows better generalization in front of unlabelled data and increases the model's robustness whenever the labelled data are scarce. Based on these metrics the model was tested on several instances with relatively encouraging performance. TED-STGN's assessment ratings were 94.7% accuracy, 95.3% precision and 92.1% recall for the identification of pancreatic cancer.

articleTitle: A Reconfiguration of an MPBR Array to Improve PV System Performance Under PSC
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Partial shading causes uneven levels of irradiance on the PV array. Uneven distribution of sunlight causes mismatch losses in PV modules connected in series. A significant problem for photovoltaic (PV) systems is partial shadowing, which reduces total efficiency. There have been several physical relocation techniques studied to reduce the negative effects of partial shade on PV arrays. In the previous study, it has been seen that the Puzzle Based Reconfiguration (PBR) approach yielded good results. However, when an in-depth study was conducted, a drawback in that approach was noticed. Specifically, regardless of the type of PV array used, there was no relocation or reconfiguration possible for the 1st and last columns. This meant that the PBR formulation only occurred in the middle, and no changes were made to the 1st and last columns, thus preventing the reduction of shading effects effectively. This paper presents a novel method for physically reconfiguring PV modules in a photovoltaic array called Modified Puzzle Based Reconfiguration (MPBR) in which every cells of PV array gets distributed. The goal of this research is to increase PV array power production while reducing the effects of partial shade. The effectiveness of the MPBR method is evaluated against traditional array configurations and PBR under various shadowing conditions. To assess the effectiveness of MPBR arrangements, key parameters such as Global Maximum Power (GMP), Mismatch Loss (ML), and Fill Factor (FF) have been analyzed. This detailed evaluation highlights the benefits regarding the physical reconfiguration of MPBR method in mitigating partial shading effects, resulting in lower ML compared to traditional methods. For this evaluation, MATLAB Simulink has been used to model a 6×6 PV array.

articleTitle: Modelling and Comparative Analysis of Robust Fuzzy Controllers for LFC of an Islanded AC Microgrid
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The innovative research work presented in this manuscript addresses different Fuzzy ruled based controllers as closed frequency stabilization loop of an energy efficiented stand alone Microgrid. The Microgrid model recommended for this investigation is single area based where several distributed generation (DG) featured power producing setups are assembled together. After assembling all DG s to a common platform, the established grid is known as the microgrid. The term microgrid comes from the micro-MW generating capability of the this grid by combining all capacity of all connected individual DGs. The DGs like wind electricity plant, Solar photovoltaic (PV) electricity generating system, micro-tubine, Fuel-cell, Geo-thermal, diesel-generator and thermo-electric generation system. The microgrid is also incorporated with energetic power accumulating banks like battery bank, Super-capacitor (ultra-capacitors) and flywheel system. The microgrid faces frequency instability problem when load dynamics and wind, solar power uncertainties come to the picture. The LFC makes an accurate control strategy to build quick stability over frequency dynamic. The LFC employs several fuzzy ruled controller such as conventional Fuzzy-PID (F-PID), Fractional ordered Fuzzy-PID (FO-FPID), Multi-stage Fuzzy PID (MS-FPID) and an ideal Type-2 Fuzzy PID (T2-FPID) controllers as secondary control loop for this study. The performance of all above discussed controllers are synthesized in an unique Vortex Search algorithm (VSA).

articleTitle: Monolithic and Microservice Architecture: A Sustainable Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Selecting the appropriate architectural design is essential for guaranteeing long-term sustainability and scalability in the quickly changing field of software development. The monolithic and microservice architectural concepts are examined in this study along with their advantages, disadvantages, and suitability for different use cases. When rapid development is a top priority in tightly connected systems, the monolithic architecture—which is renowned for its simplicity and ease of deployment—offers advantages. On the other hand, by decoupling services, the microservice design offers flexibility, scalability, and resilience, which makes it perfect for dispersed, complex systems. However, there are drawbacks to switching to a microservice design, including more complicated deployment, monitoring, and management. By carefully weighing the trade-offs between microservice agility and monolithic simplicity, this study compares the two methods and shows how businesses can implement a sustainable architectural plan. The results are intended to help decision-makers and software architects choose the best architecture to achieve the long-term objectives of their projects. Using comparisons based on scalability, maintainability, performance, and deployment methodologies, this article looks at the core ideas, advantages, and trade-offs of both systems. It also looks at the variables that affect the decision between different architectures and offers information on the situations in which each strategy might work well. This research attempts to assist practitioners in choosing the architecture that most closely matches the needs and growth trajectory of their application through case studies and empirical analysis.

articleTitle: A Review on Digital Twin Integration in Hybrid Microgrids: Challenges, Opportunities, and Innovations
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Recent advancements in communication technology (CT) have sparked significant interest in the cutting-edge concept of digital twin (DT), with the potential to transform the hybrid microgrid system (HMGS). In this study, the concepts and key steps involved in building a DT enabled HMGS is discussed, which necessitates for providing a complete automation and make the device smart. The goal is to explore the traditional grid problems and highlight the solutions possible through DT based techniques. Recognizing the importance of situational awareness, security, and the resilience of HMGS, a DT enabled HMG test system (DT-HMGTS) is developed in IIT-Bhubaneswar Campus by combining both DC and AC generating sources. The related physical and virtual modeling data offers readers a comprehensive perspective, enabling them to create and implement DT technology for a wide range of power system applications. Lastly, the paper delves into future horizon of DT-HMGTS.

articleTitle: Enhancing Measurement Precision in FBG Sensors Through Robust Temperature Compensation Mechanisms
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: With the development of Fiber Bragg Grating (FBG) sensors, applications such as Structural Health Monitoring (SHM) systems, aerospace systems, and medical diagnostics have become highly accurate and more demanding. However, the use of FBG sensors is limited when the temperature varies since it brings about lateral cross-sensitivity errors in performance due to the wavelength shifting with temperature changes. This paper suggests two simple methods of avoiding this extreme that are inexpensive to compute: linear regression and polynomial fitting. The better temperature compensation model is incorporated to check the overall performance. Linear regression is a straight-line fitting method that applies to data that does not exhibit much curvature in the 25% improvement in measurement accuracy. In cases where complex temperature dependencies are present, polynomial fits are offered which improves accuracy by up to 30% by accounting for the non-linear tail showing more complex characteristics. Investigations using laboratory experimental data show the success of these techniques and show that indeed polynomial fitting worked better than linear fitting in measurements that were time-varying. Relatively easy to apply and real-time capable are the unique attributes of the proposed methods in comparison to earlier approaches such as dual FBG and reference stripping techniques. The results appropriately indicate their contribution to improving the dependability of FBG sensors under various conditions. The work will go on to consider how adaptive models and machine learning can help future FBG sensor measurements become more robust.

articleTitle: AgriScan: Next-Gen Corn Leaf Disease Detection and Analysis Using Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The relentless advancement of computer science, with a focal point on Artificial Intelligence (AI), has ushered in a new era of innovation, presenting solutions to multifaceted challenges across various domains. This report delves into the transformative potential of AI, specifically leveraging deep learning techniques, to tackle a pressing issue faced by farmers during the growth and production stages of corn—accurate diagnosis of crop diseases. Conventional methods have proven inadequate, resulting in substantial production losses. This comprehensive solution is poised to empower farmers by facilitating remote monitoring and enabling the timely detection of three prevalent corn leaf diseases: leaf blight, leaf gray spot, and rust. The heart of our solution lies in the development of a sophisticated deep learning model meticulously trained on extensive datasets containing diverse instances of corn leaf diseases. This model is poised to transcend the limitations of human observation, offering an unprecedented level of accuracy in identifying and classifying diseases affecting corn crops. The deep learning model, a product of meticulous training, equips the application to detect and diagnose these diseases with remarkable precision. The potential impact on the agricultural sector is profound, with farmers gaining the ability to identify issues at an early stage, allowing for timely intervention and mitigation. In conclusion, the proposed deep learning model integrated into an android- based application represents a pioneering solution to a longstanding challenge in agriculture. As we navigate the complexities of modern farming, the fusion of AI and agriculture emerges as a beacon of progress, heralding a future where technology becomes an indispensable ally in the quest for global food security.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Wireless Power Transfer for Electric Vehicles with Integrated Constant Current and Constant Voltage Charging Capabilities
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) are the rapidly growing alternative to combustion vehicles, offering wide opportunity for research scope. However, electric vehicles face several challenges such as inadequate charging infrastructure, service availability and high battery cost. To address such challenges, the establishment of EV charging stations following the necessary standards is required and researchers need to address the challenges associated with it. Among the common methods of charging wireless method is more advantageous than the plug-in type of charging, which eliminates manual plugin chords and facilitates more safe and convenient charging. When a charging station is unavailable nearby, but another EV is ready to share the battery power, Vehicle-to-Vehicle power transfer becomes a viable solution. In the proposed method, the charging pad is placed at the front side of the EV and acts as a transmitter pad and receiver pad based on the request. The EV has an active rectifier with a boost topology, which controls the charging pad. This coupler mechanism couples with the wireless charging station or as well as another vehicle providing seamless charging architecture. The operating modes of the bi-directional converter are described, and the Constant Current/ Constant Voltage (CC/CV) charging is achieved with the load prediction-based control. Simulation analysis is carried out for a 3.3kW system and the results are represented for the proposed method.

articleTitle: Beyond the Blink: IoT's Next-Gen Drowsiness Detection System for Drivers
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Drowsiness during driving includes high risks for the driver, the co-passengers, and the other people on the road. Advance Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS) have been proposed to reduce these risks. This work introduces a new Internet of Things (IoT) seizure detection system to improve driver safety using Raspberry Pi, which is equipped with various sensors and utilizes machine learning for real-time monitoring and analysis. Using sensor fusion technology, including monitoring yawning and eye-closing patterns, the system aims to detect early signs of driver sleepiness. Being a low-cost, versatile, and tiny device, it becomes an ideal core processor for integration into an in-car environment. Additionally, the simplicity enables seamless communication with various sensors and facilitates effective data collection. Extensive tests and simulations were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness and reliability of the proposed system for real-world driving situations. The result outcomes prove the system's accuracy and efficiency in detecting early signs of driver fatigue to enhance driver safety. The integration of Raspberry Pi and sensor fusion technology makes it economical as well as scalable approaches supporting multiple platforms.

articleTitle: A Hybrid APF Approach for Obstacle Avoidance in a 3D Environment
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This study's main objective is to look at strategies, for avoiding underwater collisions and planning trajectories while navigating around static obstacles. Traditional Artificial Potential Fields (APF) face challenges such as getting stuck in local minima, which diminishes the path's optimality. Additionally, conventional APF often results in trajectories characterized by sharp turns or sudden changes in direction, particularly in environments populated with numerous obstacles. These obstacles can significantly hinder Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) that depend on smooth trajectories for maintaining stability and control. To address these drawbacks, we present the Hybrid A* - Artificial Potential Field (HA-APF) algorithm. When using AUVs for collision avoidance duties, adherence to safety procedures is crucial. We propose an enhanced HA-APF algorithm to address this issue for efficient path planning and collision avoidance. Additionally, the A* algorithm, which has been altered to mitigate the innate problems with local optimality in the conventional APF approach, is used in conjunction with the improved APF technique. Finally, validations are conducted in three different regions with different beginning and finishing positions. These tests show how feasible and successful the suggested algorithm is in assisting AUVs in avoiding collisions while also carrying out path-planning duties. Through this work, we provide a robust tool for advancing AUV capabilities in real-world applications, ultimately allowing for more effective underwater exploration and intervention.

articleTitle: Optimizing Network Intrusion Detection Systems for IoT: Insights from Ensemble and Neural Network Models
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The rapid increase in IoT devices has resulted in a significant rise in network traffic, creating new challenges in maintaining strong cybersecurity. To effectively combat both known and unknown cyber threats, such as DoS attacks, advanced network intrusion detection systems (NIDS) in IoT environments must ensure real-time and thorough detection. This study investigates the effectiveness of various machine learning and deep learning models in identifying DoS attacks using the TON_IoT dataset, specifically focusing on its network traffic component. The employed models included ensemble classifiers like the Extra Trees Classifier and Gradient Boosting Classifier, as well as various neural network architectures, including the Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) Classifier, Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), Deep Neural Networks (DNN), and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN). The experimental findings reveal that the Gradient Boosting Classifier achieved the highest performance with a flawless accuracy of 100%, while both the Extra Trees Classifier and MLP Classifier obtained commendable outcomes with accuracies of 90%. The CNN also performed well, achieving an accuracy of 95% due to its high precision and recall metrics. Conversely, both the DNN and ANN struggled with the complexity of the dataset, resulting in lower accuracies of 68% and 38%, respectively. In summary, the findings indicate that ensemble learning techniques, particularly the Gradient Boosting Classifier, are effective in detecting DoS attacks and contribute to the development of robust NIDS tailored for IoT contexts. Thus, this research adds valuable perspectives on creating efficient intrusion detection systems to address the distinctive security challenges commonly faced by IoT networks.

articleTitle: Exploring Traffic Signal Control: A Comprehensive Survey on Reinforcement Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Urban traffic congestion at intersections poses a significant challenge, leading to inefficiencies in traffic flow and increased wait times. Traditional fixed-timer traffic signal systems fail to adapt to fluctuating traffic volumes, exacerbating congestion during peak hours and leading to unnecessary delays during off-peak hours. Reinforcement Learning (RL) offers a promising solution by enabling traffic signal control systems to dynamically adjust signal timings based on real-time data. This paper surveys the current state of traffic signal control systems, highlighting the advantages of RL-based methods and presenting future directions for improvement, including the integration of Internet of Things (IoT) devices, advanced RL algorithms, and enhanced pedestrian detection systems. Through a comparative analysis of existing methods, we propose future enhancements that can further optimize urban traffic management.

articleTitle: Healthcare System Using IoT and Health Monitor Website
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Technological advancements and the miniaturization of sensors have prompted initiatives to implement these innovations in diverse fields, aiming to enhance the standard of living for individuals. A notable domain that has adopted this technology is the healthcare industry. Individuals requiring healthcare services often encounter high costs, a situation that is especially prevalent in developing nations. Consequently, the project aims to address a pressing healthcare issue that societies are currently facing, with the primary goal of developing a remote healthcare system. By analyzing data via a website, healthcare professionals or guardians can monitor a patient's health status from outside the hospital environment. In this initiative, we have designed a tailored Internet of Things (IoT) framework specifically aimed at healthcare applications. The project's aim was to establish a Health Analyzing System that employs locally sourced sensors, ensuring its cost-effectiveness for potential large-scale production. The suggested model gets the sensor data via the Arduino Nano microcontroller and sends the data to the cloud for processing and analysis., thereby facilitating remote access. The feedback actions derived from the analyzed data can be viewed on the website associated with the device.

articleTitle: Defensive Strategies Against CAN-Bus Infiltrations
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The Computerization of vehicles rapidly accelerated, and as vehicle networks link to external networks, automotive security becomes a critical issue. The Controller Area Network (CAN) bus is the most widely used internal control network in automobiles, facing growing vulnerabilities. With the development of networked and self-driving technology, the sealing nature of automotive internal control networks is eroding, leaving the security standards inadequate by modern benchmarks. This paper aims to provide a brief overview of the defence strategies against CAN Bus infiltrations, identify current limitations to these existing strategies, and discuss the challenges of enhancing the security in automotive embedded systems.

articleTitle: Reviewing the Role of Blockchain Enhanced Smart Contract Security Framework in Healthcare
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Blockchain technology, implemented via smart contracts, provides significant improvements in data security, transparency, and automation within healthcare applications. Smart contracts are inherently unsuitable for critical healthcare settings. This is due to vulnerabilities such as reentrancy attacks, overflow concerns, and unauthorized access to sensitive data. This study introduces the Blockchain Enhanced Smart Contract Security Framework (BESCSF) to enhance the security of smart contracts in healthcare applications. Present research is making use of hybrid security architecture. Such architecture incorporates sophisticated cryptographic methods, secure coding standards, and real-time monitoring. The suggested architecture has an adaptive hybrid approach. This approach uses machine learning to predict potential vulnerabilities. Present work prioritizes resource allocation for auditing and safeguarding smart contracts. This paradigm is capable to enhance the efficacy and precision of security measures. Present work evaluates the framework's performance, contract execution accuracy along with ability to reduce security breaches. It is performed via a series of tests and simulations. The hybrid method significantly enhances vulnerability detection accuracy by 15%. Moreover present research reduces execution time by 20% compared to traditional security solutions. Healthcare applications are considered in preset research papers that are capable to prioritizing security, efficiency, and regulatory compliance. Research work considers medical supply chain monitoring, patient data management, and insurance claims. Present work would find the method ideal. Thus, it also enhances trust and scalability.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Study of the Advanced Encryption Standard (AES) for Secure Communications
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: AES is a popular symmetric encryption algorithm and sophisticated encryption standard that is used to protect digital communications across mobile devices, cloud storage, and the Internet of Things. The SubBytes, ShiftRows, MixColumns, and AddRoundKey transformations make up the full AES structure. Additionally, there are methods for enlarging keys with all possible key sizes—128, 192, and 256 bits. Performance analysis of AES in various computing environments emphasizes its usability in highspeed applications and very constrained environments such as those in IoT. Based on this analysis, it's confirmed that AES remains the versatile and secure option available for modern encryption needs; hence, it shows more insight into its continuous usage and implications for the next cryptographic advancements in secure communications.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Battery Management System in an Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) play a pivotal role in addressing the challenges of present-day needs related to the reduction of greenhouse gas emissions and reliance on fossil fuels. EVs contribute to clean air quality, mitigate climate change, and promote sustainability through the integration of renewable technologies. Besides, it has become economical due to its lower operating costs. Hence, EVs foster a shift towards a robust, resilient, and eco-friendly transport sector and create scopes for innovation in green technologies. The role of a Battery Management System (BMS) becomes impertinent in the case of EVs as it is the main factor for the proper operation of EVs. There is a remarkable scope for enhanced battery performance in EVs for more reliability and endurance. Hence, research and development in BMS as well as its temperature regulation are therefore major fields of concern. In the present study, a BMS was designed and simulated for efficient charging and discharging addressing different battery faults by maintaining its temperature to reasonable limits. Results showed enhanced performance of the BMS with reasonable SoC, steady voltage, and current profile. Improved battery performance leads to a more efficient driving experience as well as fast charging capability thereby reducing the cost involved and enhancing the sustainability of the system.

articleTitle: Utilizing Deep Convolutional Neural Network and Local Binary Pattern Fusion for Plant Leaf Disease Identification: An Integrated Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Precise detection of plant diseases is essential in agriculture to maximize crop management and yield. The present study presents an innovative approach that integrates convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with local binary patterns (LBPs) in order to enhance the categorization of plant leaf diseases. The intricacy of plant disease images complicates the evaluation of their many features by conventional approaches. To solve this, the suggested technique utilizes the strengths of both CNNs and LBPs. The CNN component is highly effective in extracting discriminative features from raw pictures using hierarchical representations, which are crucial for differentiating between different illness categories. Simultaneously, the LBP descriptor enhances its usefulness by acquiring intricate texture information from specific areas of the images, so providing more effectiveness in distinguishing small differences resulting from various diseases. Utilizing a feature fusion approach, the merging of CNN and LBP features merges spatial and textural data, resulting in a more thorough representation of the input images. The fusion described herein significantly improves the precision of plant disease classification. The analysis of benchmark datasets of plant leaf diseases showed that this integrated method outperforms the use of CNNs or LBPs individually in terms of classification accuracy. The research findings indicate that the suggested approach, which combines deep Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) with Linear Bayesian Processes (LBPs), provides a more efficient approach for detecting plant leaf illnesses. This, in turn, makes a substantial contribution to crop management and agricultural productivity.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Controller for the Integration of Solar PV and Battery in DC Microgrid for Rural Application
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The growing integration of Renewable Energy Sources (RES) in Distributed Generation has significantly enhanced the capabilities and reliability of modern power systems. However, the intermittent nature of solar energy necessitates the use of battery-supported systems to provide additional power backup when needed. The efficiency of a DC microgrid depends on the coordinated control of both DC and AC sources connected to it. This paper presents a DC microgrid topology that integrates Solar Photovoltaic (PV) systems, batteries, and a three-phase AC grid to ensure uninterrupted power system operation. A DC-DC boost converter, integrated with the Perturb and Observe (P&O) algorithm, is used to achieve maximum power point tracking (MPPT) for the solar PV system. Additionally, a bidirectional DC-DC buck-boost converter is employed with the battery to maintain continuous operation despite fluctuations in solar irradiance. A key advantage of this proposed configuration is the reduction in the battery's charging and discharging cycles, thereby extending its lifespan. Furthermore, the DQ control strategy is applied to the active bridge rectifier to ensure unity power factor operation when interfacing with the three-phase grid. The system is modeled and simulated using MATLAB/Simulink, incorporating the design parameters of the boost and bidirectional converters, as well as the solar PV and battery models. The developed controller demonstrates satisfactory performance under both steady-state and dynamic conditions.

articleTitle: Robust Classification of Indian Currency: Deep Learning Solutions for Modern Financial Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The paper introduces an innovative model for the classification of Indian currency notes, with five key denominations: Rs 10, Rs 50, Rs 100, Rs 500, and Rs 2000. Exceptional performance metrics have been achieved in the model, with precision, recall, and F1-scores of 94.34, 95.89, 95.42, 94.83, and 95.74 for Rs 10, Rs 50, Rs 100, Rs 500, and Rs 2000, respectively. The dataset had 12,800 images, and the version reached an accuracy of 95.31% while identifying Indian forex notes. These values show that the model is ideal to identify and classify every currency denomination correctly. In addition, the analysis highlighted support and support ratios with a fair distribution of each class; Rs 10 had support of 2120 (17%), Rs 50 at 2920 (23%), Rs 100 at 2620 (20%), Rs 500 at 2320 (18%), and Rs 2000 at 2820 (22%). The attained overall accuracy is as high as 98% for all classes, which is an indication of the reliability of the model in actual operation. Results indicate that the proposed model facilitates high efficiency in overcoming currency detection and verification problems, thereby paving the way toward improvements in automatic financial transaction systems. In this work, advanced classification techniques are taken as a framework for ensuring enhanced security and efficiency in currency management.

articleTitle: Preparation and Development of Polymer-Based Dielectric Composite: Influence of Agro-Waste Materials
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Developing novel dielectric materials has always been an exciting area in material research, owing to their importance, especially in the electrical and electronic industries. Materials play an essential role in every walk of life. Extracting materials from nature, processing and understanding their characteristics, and using them proficiently are living skills. It focuses on utilizing polytetrafluoroethylene (PTFE) as a matrix with varying different weight fractions of banana leaves (BL) and sugarcane bagasse (SCB) to improve capacitive energy storage and reduction of material weight. An attempt was made to choose a 10% tantalum pentoxide (Ta2O5) filler as secondary reinforcement, which was found to have a high dielectric constant and good compatibility with the existing fabrication procedure. Therefore, this work has focused on elucidating various aspects of the dielectric behavior and has been carried out on lightweight materials with high dielectric constants and low leakage currents for memory devices. The PTFE/6%(BL-SCB)/5% Ta2O5 has a high tensile strength of 46.78 MPa and improves electrical resistivity of 3.235 volts. Hence, this type of material has potential applications in producing dielectric devices like capacitors, actuators, and environmentally friendly solutions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Q-learning for Path Planning of AUV in Obstacle-Dense Environments
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Effective trajectory planning is crucial for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) in executing a variety of functions, such as emergency response and logistical support operations. Recently, the domain of dynamic trajectory planning has emerged as a significant area of scholarly inquiry, allowing AUVs to maneuver without reliance on pre-existing static data. Researchers are harnessing the principles of reinforcement learning (RL), which has gained prominence as a contemporary field of research, to address the complexities inherent in dynamic trajectory planning. In this investigation, dynamical detection and avoiding collisions methodology is proffered to facilitate navigation within an unstructured environment replete with obstacles. Firstly, we implement the Q-learning algorithm, a specialized subset within the realm of RL, to confront the challenges posed by trajectory planning in an obstacle-laden environment. At the outset, the agent undergoes training to ascertain an effective path through the environment, subsequently selecting the shortest route while circumventing collisions with obstacles. Evaluations conducted across three distinct settings are conducted to assess the efficacy of the proposed method against randomly generated starting and destination coordinates. The findings obtained reveal that the offered strategy is superior in terms of path efficiency and the duration of travel required to reach the intended destination while successfully evading collisions. The suggested strategy holds the potential to enhance underwater search and rescue operations in inundated urban locales or regions impacted by calamities. The AUVs are adept at navigating through complex and unfamiliar underwater environments, skillfully navigating around debris and obstacles, thereby enabling swift and effective identification of survivors or assessment of structural integrity.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Traditional Algorithms: A Comparative Study on Predicting Second-Hand Car Prices
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: As the used car market is rapidly increasing, the ability to accurately forecast prices have become increasingly important to both buyers and sellers. Using a variety of predictive models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Lasso Regression (LR), Ridge Regression (RR) and Neural Networks (NN), the study seeks to develop machine learning models that are accurate and reliable in determining the price of a used car. We collect data from CarsWale for the web scraping process. We are able to analyze the details of the vehicle set, such as kilometers driven, year of production, fuel type, engine capacity, and ownership details. To begin with, our methodology included data pre-processing and feature engineering, and then we implemented regression and ensemble learning models. Random Forest and Neural Networks are experiments with mathematical models, and they show forecast accuracy, while KNN is managed quite well with the noisy and multidimensional data. The amalgamation of some artificial neural networks, especially one that relies on XGBoost and LightGBM, resulted in the prediction of the prices with acceptable accuracy. The models, such as linear regression and decision trees, outperformed a hybrid framework of XGBoost and LightGBM with a peak R2 of 96.52% and error being the lowest. The results point to the advantages of coupling the different machine learning solutions to encounter the vagueness of the second-hand car pricing that is affected by factors such as the condition of the vehicle, its mileage, and market fluctuations. The paper allows individuals to explore the feasibility of their investment mostly in the area of automobiles by focusing on the used car scenario. The paper attempts to demonstrate by modeling that the models are not over-specialized for specific markets and that they are flexible and scalable in various economic setups.

articleTitle: Harmonic Fingerprinting for Power Quality Source Identification Using Tunable-Q Wavelet Transform
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The reliable operation of modern electrical grids heavily depends on the accurate identification of power quality disturbances caused by various sources such as non-linear loads, faults, and electric vehicle (EV) chargers. This study introduces an innovative approach for harmonic source identification using the Tunable-Q Wavelet Transform (TQWT), which delivers high-resolution time-frequency analysis to effectively capture and isolate harmonic components. By applying TQWT to voltage and current signals, we extract distinctive harmonic features that serve as unique signatures for different disturbance sources, including high-order harmonics from non-linear loads, low-frequency distortions from faults, and switching harmonics from EV chargers. To enhance classification accuracy, a dual-task Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is employed, simultaneously addressing both power quality event classification and location identification. Our results demonstrate that the proposed TQWT-based method, in conjunction with the dual-task CNN, outperforms traditional Fourier-based techniques, achieving higher accuracy, faster convergence, and reduced loss. This approach offers a promising solution for real-time power quality monitoring, providing valuable insights into grid disturbances and enhancing overall system reliability and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Advanced Automated Detection of Heart Diseases Using TQWT and Dual-Task Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This study introduces a cutting-edge automated system for detecting and classifying 14 types of heart diseases, including arrhythmias and myocardial infarction, using ECG signals. The methodology leverages the Tunable-Q Wavelet Transform (TQWT) for precise feature extraction and Morphological Component Analysis (MCA) with SALSA for effective signal decomposition. A novel dual-task deep learning model, enhanced by a dynamic non-stationary redundancy factor, r(t,f)r(t, f)r(t,f), achieves exceptional accuracy (99.7%) while reducing computational cost by 25% and accelerating convergence by 30%. This approach offers a transformative solution for real-time heart disease diagnosis, advancing healthcare efficiency and patient outcomes.

articleTitle: BCViMer 1.0: A Deep Network Pipeline for the Identification of Breast Cancer Using MRI Data
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Breast cancer ranks among the foremost causes of cancer-related deaths in women globally, with early diagnosis via advanced imaging techniques significantly enhancing patient outcomes. Convolutional neural networks (CNNs) demonstrate considerable potential in the automation of breast cancer detection. Nonetheless, their constrained capacity to capture global image features may hinder their performance. This study presents BCViMer 1.0, a deep learning pipeline utilizing the Vision Transformer (ViT) to overcome existing limitations and enhance breast cancer classification accuracy from MRI images. This research aimed to assess the efficacy of BCViMer 1.0 relative to established CNN architectures, specifically ResNet-50, ResNet-101, VGG-16, and VGG-19. Experimental results indicate that BCViMer 1.0 excels these CNN models, attaining an average classification accuracy that is 4.15% higher. The enhanced performance of BCViMer 1.0 is due to its capacity to capture long-range dependencies and global context in MRI images, facilitated by the self-attention mechanism of the ViT. In conclusion, BCViMer 1.0 exhibits superior diagnostic accuracy compared to conventional CNN-based models, representing a significant advancement in breast cancer detection. This study emphasizes the capabilities of Vision Transformers in medical imaging and establishes a basis for future investigation in clinical applications.

articleTitle: Early Brain Tumour Detection in MRI Images Through Hybrid Deep Learning Model
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Brain tumours are among the emerging significant health challenges that require early detection for complete management. Though the mainstay of diagnosis remains MRI, it can be applied in its interpretation with some challenges. This study investigates the potential of leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks, a form of artificial intelligence, to classify different brain tumours from MRI images with enhanced metrics. CNNs are said to provide the best currently available solution in achieving minimal preprocessing followed by feature engineering especially with respect to image analysis. Accuracy and efficiency in brain tumour diagnosis can be drastically improved by leveraging the power of AI.

articleTitle: Harmonic Fingerprinting for Power Quality Source Identification Using Non-Subsampled Contourlet Transform
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The reliable operation of modern electrical grids requires precise identification of power quality disturbances caused by various sources such as non-linear loads, faults, and electric vehicle (EV) chargers. This study introduces an advanced approach for harmonic source identification using the Non-Sub sampled Contourlet Transform (NSCT), a method known for its superior time-frequency resolution and ability to capture multi-scale, directional features. By applying NSCT to voltage and current signals, we extract unique harmonic patterns that effectively distinguish between disturbance sources, including high-order harmonics from non-linear loads, low-frequency distortions from faults, and switching harmonics from EV chargers. To improve classification accuracy, a dual-task Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used, addressing both the classification of power quality events and the identification of fault locations. The results show that the proposed NSCT-based method, combined with the dual-task CNN, outperforms traditional Fourier-based techniques, offering faster convergence, higher classification accuracy, and minimal loss. This integrated approach provides a powerful tool for real-time power quality monitoring, enhancing grid reliability and operational efficiency while enabling accurate source identification in complex power systems.

articleTitle: Fault Analysis of an Inverter Interfaced Multi-Location DG Based Microgrid Under Grid Integration
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: This research paper presents the current and voltage level of an inverter interfaced multi-location distributed generation (DG) based power system under fault and pre-fault scenarios. The DG system simple comprises photo-voltaic cells in integration with voltage source converter (VSC). The integration of the PV based DG system with existing grid is done through current control mode of the PV set. The fault current level of a conventional grid is normally 8 to 10 times of the rated current. In inverter interfaced electrical grid, the fault current restricted to 2 to 3 times of the rated current which may lead to mal operation of the installed relay. This research assignment focuses over voltage and current level at different location of an inverter interfaced grid under a symmetric L-L-L fault scenario. The suggested current controller has anticipated a PI control scheme for making necessary control action in DG set. Since, the grid rating is high as compared to each individual DG, the major contribution for the fault current is shared by the utility grid. Finally, it is also observed that the fault current level is restricted below 3 times of the rated current due to penetration of VSC based inverter.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Hybrid Algorithm for Smooth AUV Path Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The development of effective multi-objective optimization strategies for Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) operating in uncharted territories constitutes a considerable challenge. This endeavor necessitates the simultaneous minimization of travel time, reduction of path length, enhancement of navigational safety, and smoothing of trajectories. In light of these challenges, this research presents an innovative real-time path planning framework that seamlessly integrates Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with Simulated Annealing (SA), thereby enhancing AUV navigation within static environments. The PSO algorithm is utilized to generate optimal temporary waypoints across the scenarios examined, by balancing the crucial optimization parameters. Subsequently, an optimal path is formulated, informed by both the initial and terminal points. The efficacy of the proposed methodology is assessed through simulations conducted across three distinct maps. Each obstacle map demonstrates varying densities of obstacles. The outcomes of these simulations emphasize the robustness and adaptability of the proposed strategy, highlighting its ability to formulate optimal paths within complex underwater environments, irrespective of the arrangement of obstacles. The AUVs display remarkable agility in maneuvering through intricate underwater landscapes, adeptly avoiding debris and obstacles while preserving operational efficiency. This enhanced path planning technique not only elevates the responsiveness of the AUVs during critical missions—such as search and rescue operations and structural assessments—but also significantly bolsters their overall navigational safety. Through this research, we introduce a formidable tool for enhancing AUV capabilities in practical applications, ultimately facilitating more efficient underwater exploration and intervention.

articleTitle: Efficiency Improvement in Electric Vehicle Battery Management Using Fuzzy Logic and Pi Controllers
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: An extensive analysis of the charging and discharging properties of batteries used in electric vehicle (EV) vehicles is presented in this work. A comparison is made between the Lithium-Ion battery and other battery types used in electric vehicles. In order to examine factors like efficiency, safety, and thermal management, the application of Battery Management Systems (BMS) with various battery types is investigated and the results are compared. The results prompted further investigation into the features of Lithium-Ion batteries, including voltage, state of charge, and health. The maximum battery voltage is computed using the voltage versus State of Charge (SoC) graph after the one and two RC networks of the equivalent circuit models were examined. The desire for more environmentally friendly and sustainable modes of transportation is what is driving the electric vehicle (EV) industry's rapid development. The battery, which is central to this evolution, is a major factor in vehicle performance, range, and user experience. Lithium-ion batteries are the preferred battery type for modern EVs due to its high energy density, long cycle life, and rapid charging speed. This study examines the features of EV battery charging and discharging with an emphasis on how these aspects affect EV mobility in India and around the world. The effects of significant developments in battery management systems (BMS) and control strategies, including temperature management and regenerative braking, on battery performance and lifespan are investigated. Additionally, the combination of sluggish AC and quick DC.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enabled Examination Feedback System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: The project proposes an Examination Feedback System utilizing machine learning to automate the evaluation of subjective answers in educational assessments. The system will analyze student responses and classify them under a number of predefined topics while making sure that the feedback it generates is tailored and specific to the needs of the students. The primary goal is to ensure improved outcomes through enhanced information to students, where improvement is needed, while helping educators identify performance trends. The system is powered by DistilBERT, which is a transformer-based natural language processing model which is known for its efficiency and contextual knowledge. The proposed system differs from previous manual grading systems in that it offers data-driven information while addressing confidentiality issues with a computationally efficient design. Thus, the examination process becomes scalable, accurate, and data-driven in satisfying the demands of upstream education systems with very limited computational infrastructure.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Driven Forecasting of Power Generation in Agri-Photovoltaics System
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Solar PV technology is increasingly recognized as a pivotal solution in combating climate change and transitioning towards renewable energy. This paper delves into the intricate landscape PV energy, with a specific focus on predictive modeling of Agri-photovoltaic (APV). This paper implements several Machine Learning models such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Gaussian Process Regression (GPR), Linear Regression (LR), Decision Tree (DT), and Support Vector Machine (SVM) to predict the APV power generation of a APV project which is located in Gujarat, India. All models underwent evaluation using root mean square error (RMSE), mean square error (MSE), mean absolute error (MAE) and the coefficient of determination (R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>). Based on the model performance metrics, LR, GPR and ANN model surpassed all others for APV. The SVM model demonstrated characteristics of over fitting. Despite a few research studies predicting ground-mounted PV energy yield, there is limited to no research on APV energy yield prediction in the South Asian region. Hence, this paper presents a novel approach to forecasting APV energy yield using the above-mentioned machine learning regression models.

articleTitle: KIIT at a Glance
publicationTitle: 2025 3rd IEEE International Conference on Industrial Electronics: Developments & Applications (ICIDeA)
abstract: Kalinga Institute of Industrial Technology (KIIT), a household name in the education sector, has become a sought-after destination in India for professional studies. It is admired all over for the quality of its academic courses, its community outreach work and as a university of compassion and humanitarianism. It has become a case study because no other educational institution in India has grown in its scope and scale as much as KIIT has in a short span of 25 years. Its incredible transformation is truly a journey from Soil to Silver. KIIT started in 1992-93 as an Industrial Training Institution. However, 1997 is considered the base year for the University as undergraduate and postgraduate courses in Engineering, Management and Computer Applications were added. In 2007, many new schools were added to its umbrella - School of Law, Biotechnology, Medical Sciences, Dental Sciences, Nursing, Mass Communication, Film and Media, Fashion and KIIT International School. Since then, there has been no looking back! Today, KIIT offers professional education to around 40,000 students from across India. This includes 2000 international students from 65 countries. The alumni of KIIT, over a lakh of them, have made their mark in their respective careers in academics, corporate organisations, civil services and enterprise.
